definition_zh: 多雾的；雾蒙蒙的；模糊不清的；朦胧的；含泪的
definition_en: full of mist, so that things are seen dimly and are hard to see clearly
core_image: 清晨湖面浮着一层薄雾，远处的山只剩下淡淡的轮廓
scene: 雨后清早，山脚下到处是雾，看不清路的尽头。After the rain, the valley stayed misty until the sun rose.
sceneCN: 这里 misty 是「多雾的、雾蒙蒙的」（第 1 个义项：空气里充满薄雾，看东西发虚）；句意：雨后山谷一直雾蒙蒙的，直到太阳升起。

pos.zh: 多雾的；雾蒙蒙的；模糊不清的

derivatives.zh: 由 misty 去掉形容词词尾 -y 得到，义为「薄雾」
misty 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「雾蒙蒙地；模糊地」
misty 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「雾气；模糊」

senses.title: Full of mist, hard to see through
senses.definition: covered with thin cloud near the ground, so that distant things look pale and unclear
senses.definitionCN: 地面附近布满薄雾，远处的东西显得发白而不清楚
senses.example: The hills were misty all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 整个上午山间都雾蒙蒙的。
senses.why: The noun mist names thin cloud near the ground, and the suffix -y turns it into a description of surface condition.
senses.whyCN: 名词 mist 指贴近地面的薄雾，词尾 -y 把它变成描述状态或表面的形容词，所以 misty 就是「被薄雾笼罩的」。

senses.title: Blurred and unclear
senses.definition: unclear and lacking sharp detail, like a shape seen through fog
senses.definitionCN: 模糊、缺少清晰细节，像隔着雾看轮廓一样
senses.example: The photo shows a misty outline of the castle.
senses.exampleCN: 照片里城堡只剩一个朦胧的轮廓。
senses.why: If mist blurs the landscape, the word easily moves from the weather to any picture or memory without sharp edges.
senses.whyCN: 既然雾气会把景色弄得模糊，这个词就从天气自然转到任何没有清晰边缘的画面或记忆上。

senses.title: Filled with tears
senses.definition: with eyes full of tears, so that sight seems dim
senses.definitionCN: 眼里含着泪水，视线因此变得模糊
senses.example: Her eyes turned misty at the end of the film.
senses.exampleCN: 电影结尾时她眼眶湿润了。
senses.why: Tears work like fog on a window, so the same blurring image shifts from weather to emotion.
senses.whyCN: 泪水像窗上的雾气一样让视线发虚，于是同一个「模糊」意象从天气转到了情绪上。

intro.en: Misty is formed from mist plus the adjective suffix -y, and mist goes back to Old English and related Germanic forms.
intro.cn: misty 由名词 mist 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，而 mist 可追溯到古英语及相关的日耳曼语形式。

items.en: Reconstructed forms such as mistaz are thought to mean a light cloud or haze.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式如 mistaz 表示轻云或薄雾。

items.en: Mist names fine rain or a light fog in Old English.
items.cn: 古英语 mist 指细雨或薄雾。

items.en: Mist and its related forms spread through Middle English texts.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，mist 及其相关形式在文本中流行。

items.en: The adjective misty, formed with -y, appears beside the noun.
items.cn: 加词尾 -y 构成的形容词 misty 与名词并行出现。

items.en: Modern English extends misty to blurred images, memories, and teary eyes.
items.cn: 现代英语把 misty 扩展到模糊的图像、记忆与含泪的眼睛。

note.en: Misty belongs to the mist family and sits near foggy, hazy, and vague in meaning.
note.cn: misty 属于 mist 词族，在语义上与 foggy、hazy、vague 相近。

entries.definition: thin cloud or fog near the ground
entries.definitionCN: 薄雾；雾气

entries.definition: in a foggy or blurred way
entries.definitionCN: 雾蒙蒙地；模糊地

entries.definition: the state of being misty
entries.definitionCN: 朦胧；雾气

entries.definition: full of thick fog that blocks the view
entries.definitionCN: 雾重的；能见度低的

entries.definition: slightly cloudy with heat or dust in the air
entries.definitionCN: 朦胧的；雾霾般的

entries.definition: not clearly expressed or remembered
entries.definitionCN: 模糊的；含糊的

normalIntro.en: Misty is simply the noun mist wearing the adjective coat -y.
normalIntro.cn: misty 就是给名词 mist 披上形容词外衣 -y。

normal.en: Mist plus -y yields misty, just as fog plus -y yields foggy.
normal.cn: mist 加 -y 得到 misty，正如 fog 加 -y 得到 foggy。

normal.en: A misty morning is a morning when mist fills the air.
normal.cn: a misty morning 就是空气里充满雾气的清晨。

normal.en: Misty weather makes driving hard because the road looks blurred.
normal.cn: misty weather 让开车变难，因为路面看起来模糊。

normal.en: Misty also pairs with images and memories that lack sharp edges.
normal.cn: misty 也常与缺少清晰边缘的图像和记忆搭配。

normal.en: Compare misty with foggy: misty is lighter, foggy is thicker.
normal.cn: 对比 misty 与 foggy：misty 雾轻，foggy 雾重。

abstract.en: Picture a valley wrapped in white gauze.
abstract.cn: 想象山谷被一层白纱裹住。

abstract.en: Think of a photo taken through a steamed-up window.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着一层起雾的玻璃拍照。

abstract.en: See tears filling the eyes until the room blurs.
abstract.cn: 想象眼泪涌上来，整个房间变模糊。

examples.en: It was a misty morning and the ferry moved slowly.
examples.cn: 那是个雾蒙蒙的清晨，渡船开得很慢。

examples.en: The old photographs give her only misty memories of the town.
examples.cn: 那些旧照片只让她对这座小镇留下模糊的记忆。

examples.en: His eyes were misty as he read the letter.
examples.cn: 读那封信时，他的眼眶湿润了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迷死他」——美人隔雾看，朦胧得迷死人；misty 就是「雾蒙蒙、看得迷糊」；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 mist（薄雾、细雨）加形容词词尾 -y → misty；核心义「被薄雾笼罩而看不真切」，词源语言见各阶段考查，重构形式仅为一般考证。

sensesIntro.en: Misty starts as a weather word for air full of thin cloud, then spreads to images that lack sharp edges, and finally to eyes blurred by tears.
sensesIntro.cn: misty 首先是天气词，指空气里充满薄雾；继而推广到没有清晰边缘的图像；最后指被泪水模糊的眼睛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin veil of fog over a distant hill, leaving only a pale outline.
core.cn: 核心意象：远山被一层薄雾罩住，只剩淡淡轮廓。

branches.en: The literal weather sense describes air full of thin mist.
branches.cn: 字面天气义描述充满薄雾的空气。

branches.en: The blurring sense covers pictures, outlines, and memories.
branches.cn: 模糊义覆盖画面、轮廓与记忆。

branches.en: The tearful sense transfers the fog image to crying eyes.
branches.cn: 含泪义把雾的意象转移到哭泣的眼睛上。

branches.en: A misty day and a misty photo share the same soft, glowing light.
branches.cn: 雾天与朦胧照片共享同一种柔和发亮的观感。

branches.en: Both a blurred memory and teary eyes lose sharp focus.
branches.cn: 模糊的记忆与含泪的眼睛都失去了清晰焦点。

intro.en: Misty is a Germanic weather adjective built on mist with the suffix -y, and it keeps close family ties to mist, mistily, and mistiness.
intro.cn: misty 是以日耳曼语系的天气名词为底加词尾 -y 构成的形容词，与 mist、mistily、mistiness 关系紧密。

latinIntro.en: Misty has no Latin parent; Latin nebula is a distant cousin in meaning only.
latinIntro.cn: misty 没有拉丁语直接来源；拉丁语 nebula 只是在意义上相近。

items.meaning: thin cloud or fog near the ground
items.example: Mist rises from the lake at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 黎明时薄雾从湖面升起。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y changes mist into misty.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 mist 变成 misty。

items.example: The suffix -y keeps the weather sense alive.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 保留了天气含义。

items.example: The lamps glowed mistily in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 雨中灯光雾蒙蒙地亮着。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms adverbs from adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.example: Mistiness made the valley quiet and grey.
items.exampleCN: 雾气让山谷安静而灰白。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms nouns from adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Foggy is the heavier partner of misty.
items.exampleCN: foggy 是 misty 的加重版。

items.example: Hazy skies often follow hot days.
items.exampleCN: 炎热的日子常常接着雾蒙蒙的天空。

items.example: Vague memories feel like a misty window.
items.exampleCN: 模糊的记忆就像一扇起雾的窗。

definition_zh: 螨虫；小虫；极少量；小家伙；旧时的小硬币
definition_en: a very small creature like a tiny spider, or a very small amount of something
core_image: 放大镜下一只几乎看不见的微小生物，在绒毛上缓慢爬动
scene: 床垫缝隙里藏着肉眼看不见的小虫，会让人皮肤发痒。Dust mites hide in the mattress and make some people sneeze.
sceneCN: 这里 mite 是「螨虫」（第 1 个义项：极小的节肢动物，常藏在灰尘与织物里）；句意：尘螨藏在床垫里，让一些人打喷嚏。

derivatives.zh: 由古英语 mihtig 演变而来，义为「强大的」，与本词形近而语源不同
mite 加 -infested 构成复合形容词，义为「布满螨虫的」

senses.title: A very small arachnid
senses.definition: any of many tiny eight-legged creatures, such as those living in dust or on plants
senses.definitionCN: 许多极小的八足小生物，例如生活在灰尘或植物上的螨虫
senses.example: Washing the sheets hot kills most dust mites.
senses.exampleCN: 用热水洗床单可以杀死大部分尘螨。
senses.why: The old word for a tiny crawling creature narrowed in science to a whole group of eight-legged mites.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里泛指「极小的爬虫」的词，在科学语境中收窄为整类八足螨虫。

senses.title: Said as a small amount
senses.definition: a very little amount, often in fixed phrases such as a mite
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点量，常见于 a mite 一类固定说法
senses.example: The soup could use a mite more salt.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤可以再加一点点盐。
senses.why: Once a mite names something almost invisible, the same word freely measures any small quantity.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词已经指几乎看不见的东西时，它自然就用来量度任何极小的数量。

senses.title: A small child, kindly
senses.definition: a small child or person thought of with affection or pity
senses.definitionCN: 带着疼爱或怜惜称呼的小孩或小个子
senses.example: The poor little mite was shivering in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这个可怜的小家伙在雨里发抖。
senses.why: Smallness is again the link, but now the tiny thing is a child who calls for care.
senses.whyCN: 连接点仍是「小」，但这里的小东西是需要照顾的孩子。

senses.title: An old coin and its widow
senses.titleCN: 旧时小硬币；寡妇的一文钱
senses.definition: a small coin of little value in older English, famous from the biblical widow
senses.definitionCN: 旧时英语中一种面值很小的小硬币，因《圣经》中的寡妇故事而著名
senses.example: The widow gave two mites, all she had.
senses.exampleCN: 寡妇投入两个小钱，那是她的全部。
senses.why: Translators used the word for a coin so small that it matched the insect, giving the widow story its English name.
senses.whyCN: 译者用这个表示小虫的词来翻译一种极小的钱币，寡妇的故事因此在英语里留下了这个名字。

intro.en: Mite, meaning a tiny creature, comes from Old English mite and is related to similar words in other Germanic languages; the coin sense entered through Bible translation.
intro.cn: 表示微小生物的 mite 来自古英语 mite，与其他日耳曼语中的近形词有关；硬币义则经由《圣经》翻译进入英语。

items.en: Reconstructed forms such as miton are thought to mean a tiny insect or small creature.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构形式如 miton 表示极小的昆虫或小生物。

items.en: Mite names a small insect or tick.
items.cn: 古英语 mite 指小昆虫或蜱类。

items.en: The word also starts to mean a small coin in biblical contexts.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，该词在《圣经》语境中开始兼指小硬币。

items.en: Bible translations fix the widow coin sense in English.
items.cn: 《圣经》译本把寡妇的小钱义固定进英语。

items.en: Zoology uses mite for an order of tiny eight-legged creatures, and colloquial usage keeps the small-amount and small-child senses.
items.cn: 现代动物学用 mite 指一类八足微小生物，口语里则保留「一点点」和「小家伙」的用法。

note.en: Mite is a tiny-creature word that also measures small amounts; it is easily confused with might in spelling and by sound alone.
note.cn: mite 既是微小生物的词，也可量度很小的量；它在拼写与发音上与 might 极易混淆。

entries.definition: past tense of may, also meaning physical power
entries.definitionCN: may 的过去式，也指力量；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to hit hard
entries.definitionCN: 猛击；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a white ant-like insect
entries.definitionCN: 白蚁；含相同的词尾拼写，但来自不同的构词，与 mite 词源无关

entries.definition: a small blood-sucking arachnid
entries.definitionCN: 蜱虫

entries.definition: a tiny spot or particle
entries.definitionCN: 小点；极少量

entries.definition: an extremely small part of a thing
entries.definitionCN: 极小的份儿；一丁点

normalIntro.en: Mite covers whatever is tiny, from the creature in a mattress to the salt in a soup.
normalIntro.cn: mite 覆盖一切「极小」的东西，从床垫里的虫子到汤里的一撮盐。

normal.en: Dust mite is the most common collocation and names the indoor creature.
normal.cn: dust mite 是最常见的搭配，指室内的尘螨。

normal.en: A mite more salt means just a little more salt.
normal.cn: a mite more salt 就是再来一点点盐。

normal.en: A mite tired means slightly tired, a gentle way of softening a complaint.
normal.cn: a mite tired 就是有点累，是委婉弱化抱怨的说法。

normal.en: Poor little mite shows affection, not disgust.
normal.cn: poor little mite 表达的是心疼，而不是嫌弃。

normal.en: Mite and might sound the same but behave differently: one is a noun, the other a modal or a noun of power.
normal.cn: mite 与 might 同音，但用法不同：前者是名词，后者是情态动词或表示力量的抽象名词。

abstract.en: Hold a magnifying glass over a pillow and see tiny creatures walk.
abstract.cn: 把放大镜对着枕头，看见小生物在走。

abstract.en: Watch a single grain of salt dissolve in soup.
abstract.cn: 看一颗盐粒在汤里化开。

abstract.en: Picture a shivering child wrapped in a big coat.
abstract.cn: 想象一个裹着大外套、瑟瑟发抖的孩子。

examples.en: Mites live in bedding and feed on dead skin.
examples.cn: 螨虫住在床上用品里，以皮屑为食。

examples.en: The path is a mite steep for an elderly walker.
examples.cn: 对年迈的散步者来说，这条路有点陡。

examples.en: She gave her last coin, a mite, to the fund.
examples.cn: 她把最后一枚小钱捐给了这个基金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埋它」——太小了，扫着扫着就埋起来看不见了；mite 就是「几乎看不见的小东西」；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 mite（极小昆虫、蜱类）← 一般考证的日耳曼语重构形式；小硬币义随《圣经》译本进入英语，核心义「极小之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Mite begins as the name of a tiny creature, then measures any small amount, then addresses a small child, and finally names a tiny coin.
sensesIntro.cn: mite 最初是微小生物的名字，随后用来量度任何小量，再到呼唤小孩，最后指极小的钱币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a creature almost too small to see, crawling across a pillow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只几乎看不见的小生物在枕头上爬行。

branches.en: The scientific sense narrows the old tiny-creature word to eight-legged mites.
branches.cn: 科学义把古老的「小生物」一词收窄为八足螨虫。

branches.en: The amount sense borrows the insect to say just a little.
branches.cn: 量义借用这种虫子来说「只有一点点」。

branches.en: The child sense softens smallness into affection.
branches.cn: 小孩义把「小」柔化成怜爱。

branches.en: An invisible creature and an invisible amount share the same scale.
branches.cn: 看不见的生物与看不见的量共享同一个尺度。

branches.en: A little child and a little coin were both called mite from the same sense of smallness.
branches.cn: 小孩子与小钱币都借「小」的意思被称为 mite。

intro.en: Mite is a short Germanic noun with technical compound partners such as dust mite, and its family is thin: the main derivatives are compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: mite 是简短的日耳曼语名词，可与 dust 等技术词组成复合词；它的词族较薄，派生主要靠复合而非词尾。

latinIntro.en: Mite has no Latin source; the Latin word acarus is used in zoology for the same group of creatures.
latinIntro.cn: mite 没有拉丁语来源；动物学中同一种群用拉丁词 acarus 表示。

items.example: Mite names the creature in bedding and soil.
items.exampleCN: mite 指生活于床品和土壤中的小生物。

items.example: The suffix -s forms mites.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成表示复数的 mites。

items.meaning: a mite living in household dust
items.example: Dust mite is the common allergenic one.
items.exampleCN: dust mite 是常见的过敏原。

items.meaning: a mite living in fresh water
items.example: Water mite swims in ponds and streams.
items.exampleCN: water mite 在池塘和溪流里游动。

items.example: The suffix -infested forms mite-infested.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -infested 构成 mite-infested。

items.example: The suffix -icide forms miticide for mite killers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -icide 构成意为杀螨剂的 miticide。

items.example: Mighty looks similar but has a different source.
items.exampleCN: mighty 形近，但语源不同。

items.example: Speck carries the same small-amount idea.
items.exampleCN: speck 承载同样的「小量」含义。

items.example: Atom is the ancient image of indivisible smallness.
items.exampleCN: atom 是「不可再分的小」的古老意象。

definition_zh: 动员；调动；组织起来；使移动；变为游行；使（资源）投入使用
definition_en: to organize people or resources so that they are ready for action or use
core_image: 一声号令，原本静止的人群和车辆同时起动，汇成一条流动的队伍
scene: 社区领袖在楼前挨家挨户敲门，把邻居组织起来修被风雨损坏的公园。Neighbours mobilised to repair the flooded play area.
sceneCN: 这里 mobilise 是「动员、组织起来」（第 1 个义项：把人召集起来准备行动）；句意：邻居们动员起来，修复被淹的游乐场。

derivatives.zh: mobilise 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「动员；调动」
mobilise 的词根来源，义为「可移动的；流动的」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已动员的；被调动的」

senses.title: To organize people for action
senses.definition: to bring people together and make them ready to act for a cause or problem
senses.definitionCN: 把人们聚到一起，使他们准备好为某个目标或问题采取行动
senses.example: Volunteers mobilised to clean the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者动员起来清理海滩。
senses.why: The Latin root mobilis means moveable, so mobilising people means setting a still crowd into motion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 mobilis 意为「可移动的」，所以动员人就是把静止的人群发动起来。

senses.title: To put troops or ships into position
senses.definition: to order soldiers, ships, or aircraft to prepare for fighting or a task
senses.definitionCN: 命令士兵、舰船或飞机准备作战或执行任务
senses.example: The regiment was mobilised within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 该团在一天之内便完成动员。
senses.why: Military use is the historical home of the word: moving an army from barracks to the front.
senses.whyCN: 军事用法是这个词的历史起点：把军队从营房调往前线，也就是让部队「动起来」。

senses.title: To bring resources into use
senses.definition: to gather and start using money, equipment, or data for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某个目的收集并开始使用资金、设备或数据
senses.example: The city mobilised extra funds for the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府为诊所调拨了额外资金。
senses.why: Resources that sit idle are still; mobilising them is making them move toward a goal.
senses.whyCN: 闲置的资源是静止的，调动资源就是让它们朝着目标流动起来。

senses.title: To move a joint or limb
senses.definition: to move a part of the body that has been stiff or injured, often as a medical instruction
senses.definitionCN: 活动已经僵硬或受伤的身体部位，常见于医嘱
senses.example: After the cast came off, she began to mobilise her wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 拆掉石膏后，她开始活动手腕。
senses.why: The oldest root sense is simply to set in motion, and the body is where movement is most concrete.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的词义就是「使运动」，而身体正是运动最具体的地方。

senses.title: To go out on a march or campaign
senses.titleCN: 走上街头；开展集会游行
senses.definition: of a group of people, to collect and march or campaign publicly for a cause
senses.definitionCN: 一群人聚集起来，为某个诉求公开游行或开展运动
senses.example: Students mobilised across the country for equal access.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们在全国各地发动游行，争取平等入学机会。
senses.why: When mobilising ends in the street, the verb comes to describe the march itself.
senses.whyCN: 动员的终点常常是街头，于是这个动词也用来直接描述游行本身。

intro.en: Mobilise comes from French mobiliser, which grew from Latin mobilis meaning moveable, and was first used for calling troops to arms.
intro.cn: mobilise 来自法语 mobiliser，源于拉丁语 mobilis（可移动的），最初用于征召军队。

items.en: Mobilis means moveable, from the verb movere, to move.
items.cn: mobilis 意为可移动的，源自动词 movere（移动）。

items.en: Mobile and related forms reach early French from the same root.
items.cn: mobile 及相关形式自同一词根进入早期法语。

items.en: Mobiliser is used for putting an army in the field.
items.cn: 十八世纪法语 mobiliser 用于把军队投入战场。

items.en: Mobilise enters English mainly as a military term.
items.cn: mobilise 以军事术语的身份进入英语。

items.en: Modern English extends mobilise to campaigns, funds, health care, and everyday resources.
items.cn: 现代英语把 mobilise 扩展到运动、资金、医疗与日常资源。

note.en: Mobilise belongs to the mobile and motive family, where every member carries the idea of movement; it is also close to organize and deploy.
note.cn: mobilise 属于 mobile、motive 这个词族，成员都带「动」的意味；它与 organize、deploy 意思也相近。

entries.definition: able to move or be moved easily
entries.definitionCN: 可移动的；流动的

entries.definition: a reason that makes someone act
entries.definitionCN: 动机

entries.definition: the act of organizing people or resources
entries.definitionCN: 动员；调动

entries.definition: to arrange people into a working whole
entries.definitionCN: 组织；筹办

entries.definition: to move forces or equipment into position
entries.definitionCN: 部署；调配

entries.definition: to gather people again for support
entries.definitionCN: 召集；重新聚拢支持者

normalIntro.en: Mobilise is made of the mobile root plus -ise, the ending that turns an adjective of movement into an action.
normalIntro.cn: mobilise 由表示「可移动」的词根加动词词尾 -ise 组成，把「能动的」变成「使之动」。

normal.en: Mobile means able to move, so mobilise means to set moving.
normal.cn: mobile 意为可移动的，所以 mobilise 意为使动起来。

normal.en: Mobilise resources is the standard phrase for making idle supplies available.
normal.cn: mobilise resources 是让闲置资源投入使用的标准搭配。

normal.en: British spelling uses -ise, American spelling uses -ize, but both sound alike.
normal.cn: 英式拼写用 -ise，美式拼写用 -ize，读音相同。

normal.en: Mobilise troops is the oldest military use of the verb.
normal.cn: mobilise troops 是这个动词最古老的军事用法。

normal.en: Mobilise and organise differ in focus: mobilise stresses readiness, organise stresses structure.
normal.cn: mobilise 与 organise 侧重点不同：前者强调准备就绪，后者强调结构安排。

abstract.en: Hear one whistle and watch a whole crowd start moving at once.
abstract.cn: 听一声哨响，看整群人同时开始移动。

abstract.en: See a train station fill with soldiers boarding trains.
abstract.cn: 想象火车站里挤满登车的士兵。

abstract.en: Watch dormant machines in a factory suddenly hum to life.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂里停着的机器突然轰隆启动。

examples.en: The charity mobilised thousands of volunteers after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪灾之后，这个慈善机构动员了数千名志愿者。

examples.en: The government mobilised every available resource to fight the fire.
examples.cn: 政府调动了一切可用的资源来灭火。

examples.en: Parents mobilised to keep the local library open.
examples.cn: 家长们动员起来，争取让当地图书馆继续开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫比来」——别再比来比去了，赶紧动起来集合，mobilise 就是「动员人动起来」；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mobilis（可移动的）← movere（移动）→ 法语 mobiliser（动员军队）→ 英语 mobilise，核心义「使静止者动起来」。

sensesIntro.en: Mobilise always means setting something still into motion: first people, then troops, then resources, then joints, and finally public marches.
sensesIntro.cn: mobilise 始终表示让静止者动起来：先是人，再是部队，然后是资源、关节，最后是街头的游行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single whistle setting a whole crowd into motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一声哨响，整个人群一起动起来。

branches.en: People mobilised for a cause are a crowd made ready.
branches.cn: 为某个目标动员起来的人，是一支准备就绪的人群。

branches.en: Troops are the original object that the verb moved.
branches.cn: 部队是这个动词最早被调动的对象。

branches.en: Resources are mobilised when idle supplies start to flow.
branches.cn: 当闲置物资开始流动时，资源就算被调动起来了。

branches.en: A joint and a march both end in visible movement.
branches.cn: 关节的活动与街头的游行都以可见的移动收尾。

branches.en: Mobilising a community often finishes as a public march.
branches.cn: 动员社区常常以一场公开游行为终点。

intro.en: Mobilise is built from the Latin root mobil, the verb ending -ise, and a family of mobile, mobility, and motive words.
intro.cn: mobilise 由拉丁词根 mobil、动词词尾 -ise 以及 mobile、mobility、motive 一族词共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere means to move, and mobilis means moveable; the whole family grows from that root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere 意为移动，mobilis 意为可移动的；整个词族都由此生长出来。

items.example: Movere is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: movere 是整个词族的根基。

items.example: Mobilis gives English the mobile root.
items.exampleCN: mobilis 给英语提供了表示移动的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns mobile into mobilise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 把 mobile 变成 mobilise。

items.meaning: same suffix in the American form
items.example: The spelling -ize gives mobilize.
items.exampleCN: 美式拼写 -ize 构成 mobilize。

items.example: Mobile keeps the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: mobile 保留了形容词含义。

items.example: Mobility is the noun of mobile, not of mobilise.
items.exampleCN: mobility 是 mobile 的名词形式，与 mobilise 不同。

items.example: Mobilisation is the direct noun of the verb.
items.exampleCN: mobilisation 是该动词的直接名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms mobilisation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 mobilisation。

items.example: Motive shares the Latin root of moving.
items.exampleCN: motive 共享拉丁语表示移动的词根。

items.example: Demobilise adds the prefix de- to reverse mobilise.
items.exampleCN: demobilise 加前缀 de- 表示反向。

items.example: The prefix de- reverses mobilise.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 使 mobilise 反向。

definition_zh: 嘲笑；模仿嘲弄；模拟的；仿制的；模拟考试
definition_en: to laugh at someone in an unkind way, or to pretend to be something in order to imitate it
core_image: 对着别人的动作夸张模仿，笑得前仰后合，把对方当笑话
scene: 排练厅里，年轻演员学老师走路的样子，把全班逗笑。In the rehearsal room, the young actor began to mock the teacher by copying the way he walked, which made the whole class laugh.
sceneCN: 这里 mock 是「嘲笑、模仿取笑」（第 1 个义项：用模仿的方式嘲弄某个人）；句意：排练厅里，年轻演员学着老师走路的样子来取笑他，把全班都逗笑了。

collocations.zh: 制作外观样机；搭建样板

derivatives.zh: 由 mock 加名词后缀 -ery 构成，义为「嘲弄；笑柄」
由过去分词形容词化，义为「嘲弄的；讥讽的」
由 mock 加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「嘲弄者」
由 mocking 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「嘲弄地」

senses.title: To laugh at someone by imitating them
senses.definition: to laugh at a person or thing in an unkind way, often by copying them
senses.definitionCN: 以不友善的方式取笑某人或某事，常用模仿的方式
senses.example: The other children mocked his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 其他孩子取笑他的口音。
senses.why: The word came through French from a mocking gesture or mimicry, so the core image is a person actively copying somebody to make them look foolish.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语而来，核心意象是刻意模仿别人、让对方显得可笑的动作，所以最直接的义项就是「用模仿去取笑」。

senses.title: To refuse to respect and treat as ridiculous
senses.definition: to show that an idea, rule, or threat is foolish or meaningless
senses.definitionCN: 表示某个想法、规则或威胁愚蠢或无意义，予以轻蔑对待
senses.example: The novel mocks the idea that money brings happiness.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小说嘲讽了「金钱带来幸福」这一说法。
senses.why: Once the sneering gesture is aimed at opinions rather than people, it becomes a refusal to take something seriously.
senses.whyCN: 当嘲笑的姿态从针对人转向针对观点时，就变成了「不把某事当回事」的蔑视。

senses.title: Pretending to be real
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something that is a copy or practice version of the real thing
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，描述真实的模仿品或练习用的版本
senses.example: Students sit a mock exam before the real test.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在正式考试前参加一次模拟考试。
senses.why: The idea of imitation is neutral once the mockery is removed: what is copied is a rehearsal, not a joke.
senses.whyCN: 去掉嘲笑的意味之后，「模仿」本身是中性的：被复制的是一个演练版本，而不是笑话。

senses.title: A practice examination
senses.definition: a test taken for practice before an official one
senses.definitionCN: 在正式考试之前进行的练习性测试
senses.example: She scored higher in the mock than in the real exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她模拟考的成绩比正式考试还高。
senses.why: The adjective sense became a noun in school and exam contexts, because the practice test itself is a copy.
senses.whyCN: 在校园与考试语境中，形容词义直接名词化，因为这场练习性测试本身就是一份「副本」。

senses.title: An object of ridicule
senses.definition: a person or thing that everyone laughs at
senses.definitionCN: 被人人取笑的人或事物
senses.example: His old-fashioned hat made him a mock for the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他那顶过时的帽子让他成了队里的笑柄。
senses.why: The verb also gave a noun for the person at the receiving end of the laughter.
senses.whyCN: 动词义也派生出名词，指站在嘲笑底端、被取笑的那个人。

intro.en: Mock came into English from Old French moquer, probably of Germanic origin, and the sense moved from jeering at people to copying something for practice.
intro.cn: mock 经古法语 moquer 进入英语，词源一般认为来自日耳曼语族，含义从「讥笑人」逐步延伸到「仿制出来作练习」。

items.en: A Germanic source is often proposed, but the exact root is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为有日耳曼语族来源，但确切词根存疑。

items.en: Moquer means to deride or make fun of someone.
items.cn: 古法语 moquer 意为讥笑、取笑某人。

items.en: Mock first appears meaning to jeer at a person.
items.cn: 中古英语时期首次出现，意为讥笑某人。

items.en: The adjective mock meaning imitation or counterfeit appears.
items.cn: 形容词义「仿制的、假的」在这一时期出现。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as mock battle and mock exam spread.
items.cn: mock battle、mock exam 这类固定搭配逐渐流行。

items.en: Mock becomes an everyday word for tests, interviews, and software stand-ins.
items.cn: 现代英语中 mock 成为考试、面试与软件替身等领域的常用词。

note.en: Mock is a jeering verb whose family includes mockery and mocking, and it sits near words for copying and for making fun.
note.cn: mock 是一个表示「讥笑」的动词，词族包括 mockery、mocking 等，并与表示「模仿」和「取笑」的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of laughing at someone unkindly
entries.definitionCN: 嘲弄；笑柄（由 mock 加名词后缀构成）

entries.definition: showing that you think someone is foolish
entries.definitionCN: 嘲弄的；讥讽的（mock 的分词形容词形式）

entries.definition: a person who laughs at others
entries.definitionCN: 嘲弄者（mock 加 -er 构成的施事名词）

entries.definition: to make fun of someone in a cruel way
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「嘲笑、讥讽」，比 mock 更书面

entries.definition: to laugh at someone playfully, usually without cruelty
entries.definitionCN: 戏弄；逗弄，通常不带恶意，语气比 mock 轻

entries.definition: to copy someone or something without any intention to laugh
entries.definitionCN: 模仿，不带取笑意味，中性；mock 的模仿则带讥讽

normalIntro.en: Mock is the imitation that laughs: a person copies another in order to make them look silly, and the same copying idea later becomes a practice test.
normalIntro.cn: mock 是「带笑的模仿」：一个人复制别人的样子好让对方显得可笑，后来同样的复制动作又变成了练习考试。

normal.en: To mock a person is to copy them on purpose so that others laugh.
normal.cn: mock 一个人，就是故意学他的样子让旁人发笑。

normal.en: A mock exam is a copy of the real test taken for practice.
normal.cn: mock exam 就是正式考试的复制版，用来练习。

normal.en: Mock trial and mock interview are both rehearsal situations.
normal.cn: mock trial 与 mock interview 都是演练性质的场景。

normal.en: Mockery is the noun for the laughter, mocking is the adjective that describes it.
normal.cn: mockery 是名词，指嘲弄本身；mocking 是形容词，形容嘲弄的语气。

normal.en: Mock the idea sounds stronger than disagree with, because it adds contempt.
normal.cn: mock the idea 比 disagree with 语气更强，因为它多了鄙视的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a stage clown copying a teacher behind his back for laughs.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上的小丑趁老师背过身时学他的样子逗观众笑。

abstract.en: Imagine a critic waving away a grand slogan with two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象一位批评家只用两根手指就把一句漂亮口号挥开。

abstract.en: See a cardboard stand-in of a car used for testing paints.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆纸板做成的样车，专门用来测试车漆。

examples.en: The audience mocked the speaker for his clumsy gestures.
examples.cn: 听众取笑了演讲者笨拙的手势。

examples.en: All students must pass a mock exam before applying.
examples.cn: 所有学生在申报之前都必须通过一次模拟考试。

examples.en: The team mocked the rule and ignored the new deadline.
examples.cn: 整个团队蔑视这条规定，无视了新的截止时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫客」——别当客人，别学人家样子去取笑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 moquer（讥笑）→ 中古英语 mock（讥笑某人）；词源上一般认为与日耳曼语族有关，但确切来源存疑，核心义「模仿着取笑」，后延伸出「仿制、模拟」义。

sensesIntro.en: Mock begins with a jeering imitation of a person, widens to show contempt for ideas, then turns the imitation itself into something neutral and finally into a noun for practice exams.
sensesIntro.cn: mock 先指带着讥讽地模仿一个人，再扩展为对观点表示蔑视，之后「模仿」本身变得中性，指仿制品与模拟版本，最后名词化为练习考试等。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands copying someone on purpose so that everyone laughs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手故意照着别人的样子做动作，好让所有人发笑。

branches.en: Copying a person to laugh at them is the first and basic sense.
branches.cn: 学别人的样子来取笑，是最基本的第一义项。

branches.en: Taking an idea lightly is the target shifted from person to opinion.
branches.cn: 把观点视作可笑，是取笑对象从人转移到意见的结果。

branches.en: Mock plus a noun names a copy of the real thing, with no laughter left.
branches.cn: mock 加名词时指真东西的复制品，嘲笑的意味已经消失。

branches.en: A practice examination is the noun form of the copy sense.
branches.cn: 模拟考试是「副本」义名词化而来的具体场景。

branches.en: The person being imitated and laughed at becomes a mock, a figure of fun.
branches.cn: 被人模仿取笑的那一方就变成了 mock，即笑柄。

intro.en: Mock is a single-root word borrowed from Old French, with the suffix -ery, -ing, -er, and -ly forming its family.
intro.cn: mock 是一个从古法语借来的单根词，由 -ery、-ing、-er、-ly 等后缀构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Mock has no secure Latin ancestor, so the related forms listed here are its Old French source and English family members.
latinIntro.cn: mock 没有可确证的拉丁语祖形，因此这里列出的是它的古法语来源与英语词族成员。

items.meaning: to jeer at, to make fun of
items.example: Moquer is the direct source of mock.
items.exampleCN: moquer 是 mock 的直接来源。

items.meaning: to laugh at someone by imitating them
items.example: Children often mock each other.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们常常互相取笑。

items.example: The city runs mock fire drills.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市举行模拟消防演练。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ery forms mockery from mock.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ery 把 mock 构成 mockery。

items.meaning: the act of laughing at someone
items.example: Mockery is the noun of the laughing act.
items.exampleCN: mockery 是「嘲笑」这一行为的名词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms mocker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 mocker。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms mocking.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 mocking。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms mockingly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mockingly。

items.meaning: a full-size model used for testing
items.example: A mock-up helps designers test the layout first.
items.exampleCN: 样板让设计师先测试排版效果。

latinEntries.example: Moquer passes into English as mock.
latinEntries.exampleCN: moquer 进入英语后写作 mock。
moquerie 是英语 mockery 的前身。

definition_zh: 适度；节制；缓和；审核；版务管理
definition_en: the quality of avoiding extremes, or the act of keeping something under control and within limits
core_image: 一只手把摆锤轻轻拨回中间，不让它再往左右两边荡
scene: 医生劝他喝咖啡要有节制，别一天喝太多。The doctor advised him to drink coffee in moderation instead of having several cups a day.
sceneCN: 这里 moderation 是「适度、节制」（第 1 个义项：不过量、不走极端）；句意：医生劝他喝咖啡要适度，而不是一天喝上好几杯。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语词根加词缀构成，义为「适度的；温和的」
由 moderate 加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「主持人；审核员」
由 moderate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「适度地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 moderate 构成，义为「无节制的」

senses.title: The quality of avoiding extremes
senses.definition: the habit or state of staying within sensible limits, neither too much nor too little
senses.definitionCN: 保持在合理限度内的习惯或状态，既不过多也不过少
senses.example: He eats sweets in moderation.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃甜食很有节制。
senses.why: The Latin verb moderari means to keep within measure, so the core idea is a hand holding something back from the two extremes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 moderari 意为「保持在尺度之内」，核心就是一只手把事物从两个极端往中间拉回来。

senses.title: The act of making something less extreme
senses.definition: the act of reducing the strength or force of something
senses.definitionCN: 削弱某事物的强度或力度的行为
senses.example: The report calls for moderation of the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 报告呼吁对新规定加以放缓。
senses.why: If measure is applied to something too strong, the result is a softening rather than a wholesale change.
senses.whyCN: 当「尺度」被施加到过于强烈的事物上时，结果就是缓和，而不是彻底改变。

senses.title: Checking posts and keeping them within rules
senses.definition: the work of reviewing posts, comments, or products and removing those that break the rules
senses.definitionCN: 审查帖子、评论或商品，并删除违反规则内容的工作
senses.example: The forum depends on content moderation to stay civil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论坛依靠内容审核来保持文明讨论。
senses.why: Online communities apply the same measure to speech, so the one who holds the limits is now doing review work.
senses.whyCN: 网络社区把同样的「尺度」用在言论上，于是把握尺度的人就成了做审核工作的人。

senses.title: Bringing people to a middle course
senses.definition: the process of making people less extreme in their views, especially in politics
senses.definitionCN: 使人们的观点变得不那么极端的过程，尤指政治方面
senses.example: The party has moved towards moderation in recent years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党近年来向温和靠拢。
senses.why: A middle course is the literal platform of the core image, so a person or party that avoids the extremes is described this way.
senses.whyCN: 「中间路线」正是这个核心意象的字面位置，所以避免极端的人或政党就用这个词来描述。

intro.en: Moderation comes from Latin moderatio, a governing or restraining, from moderari, to keep within measure, built on modus, a measure.
intro.cn: moderation 来自拉丁语 moderatio（调节、制约），源于 moderari（保持在尺度之内），其词根是 modus（尺度）。

items.en: Modus means a measure or limit.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、限度。

items.en: Moderari means to keep within measure or to restrain.
items.cn: moderari 意为保持在尺度之内、加以制约。

items.en: Moderatio means a restraining or governing.
items.cn: moderatio 意为节制、约束。

items.en: Moderacion passes into French with the sense of restraint.
items.cn: moderacion 以「节制」之义进入法语。

items.en: Moderation names the quality of self-control in English.
items.cn: 中古英语中 moderation 指自我克制的品质。

items.en: Moderation gains the online sense of reviewing user content.
items.cn: 现代英语中 moderation 增添了「审核用户内容」的网络新义。

note.en: Moderation is the measure noun of the moderate family, and it sits near words for restraint, balance, and control.
note.cn: moderation 是 moderate 词族中表示「尺度」的名词，与表示克制、平衡、控制的一批词相邻。

entries.definition: neither very large nor very small
entries.definitionCN: 适度的；温和的（与 moderation 同根）

entries.definition: a person who keeps a discussion or a site within limits
entries.definitionCN: 主持人；审核员（moderation 的施事名词）

entries.definition: going beyond reasonable limits
entries.definitionCN: 无节制的；过度的（否定前缀加同根形容词）

entries.definition: the act of holding yourself back
entries.definitionCN: 克制；约束，强调「忍住不做」

entries.definition: an even state between opposite forces
entries.definitionCN: 平衡，强调两边力量相当

entries.definition: the habit of never drinking too much alcohol
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「节制」，尤其指饮酒有度

normalIntro.en: Moderation is built on the Latin measure modus: to moderate is to keep to the measure, and moderation is the state of doing so.
normalIntro.cn: moderation 建在拉丁语的「尺度」modus 之上：to moderate 就是守住尺度，moderation 就是守住尺度的状态。

normal.en: In moderation means in a self-controlled amount, not too much.
normal.cn: in moderation 表示有节制地、不过量。

normal.en: Content moderation is the steady review of user posts.
normal.cn: content moderation 就是对用户帖子的持续审查。

normal.en: Moderate is to moderation what measure is to measuring: the same root in action and in state.
normal.cn: moderate 与 moderation 是同根的两个形态，一个表示动作，一个表示状态，正如 measure 之于 measuring。

normal.en: A moderator holds the limit, so the job keeps the moderator idea of holding a balance.
normal.cn: moderator 把守限度，所以「审核员」这一职位保留了「掌握平衡」的意味。

normal.en: Politicians who move towards moderation soften their positions.
normal.cn: 政客向 moderation 靠拢，就是把立场放温和。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum being stopped exactly at the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摆锤正好被停在最低点。

abstract.en: Imagine turning down a loud volume knob to a comfortable level.
abstract.cn: 想象把很响的音量旋钮调到舒服的档位。

abstract.en: See a sign at the entrance of a forum that asks for calm words.
abstract.cn: 想象论坛入口挂着一块牌子，请大家平和发言。

examples.en: Chocolate is fine if you eat it in moderation.
examples.cn: 巧克力只要适量吃就没有问题。

examples.en: The company hired a team for content moderation.
examples.cn: 这家公司组建了一个团队负责内容审核。

examples.en: Voices of moderation were ignored during the debate.
examples.cn: 辩论中温和理性的声音被忽略了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫多」——莫要多，莫要少，适量刚好；再拆「mode + ration」，按定量来分，就是节制；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度）+ moderari（保持在尺度之内）→ moderatio（节制）→ 古法语 moderacion → 英语 moderation，核心义「守住尺度、不走极端」。

sensesIntro.en: Moderation starts from the state of keeping to a measure, turns into the act of softening what is too strong, and then moves into everyday work of holding limits, from comments to politics.
sensesIntro.cn: moderation 从「守住尺度」的状态出发，转为把过强之物调缓的动作，再延伸到日常中把守限度的具体工作，从网络评论到政治立场皆是如此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that steadies a pendulum exactly at the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把摆锤稳稳定在正中间的位置。

branches.en: Staying within measure is the everyday sense of self-control.
branches.cn: 停在尺度之内，就是日常所说的自制与节制。

branches.en: Applying measure to something too strong produces softening.
branches.cn: 把尺度施加到过强之物上，就产生缓和之义。

branches.en: Holding limits online turns into the job of reviewing content.
branches.cn: 在网络空间把守限度，就变成了审核内容的具体工作。

branches.en: A group that avoids the extremes is said to move towards the middle.
branches.cn: 避开极端的群体，就被说成向中间靠拢。

branches.en: Both the softening of rules and content review reduce what goes beyond the limit.
branches.cn: 规则的放缓和内容审核，都是在削减越过界限的部分。

intro.en: Moderation is built from the Latin measure root mod- with the noun suffix -tion, and its family includes moderate, moderator, and immoderate.
intro.cn: moderation 由拉丁语「尺度」词根 mod- 加名词后缀 -tion 构成，词族包括 moderate、moderator 与 immoderate。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus means a measure, and moderari means to keep within measure, giving the whole moderate family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus 意为尺度，moderari 意为保持在尺度之内，由此生出整个 moderate 词族。

items.example: The root mod- appears in mode and module too.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mod- 也见于 mode 与 module。

items.example: Modus is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: modus 是整个词族的根基。

items.example: Moderari supplies the controlling idea.
items.exampleCN: moderari 提供了「加以控制」的含义。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion turns the action into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 把动作变作名词。

items.example: Moderation keeps the noun sense.
items.exampleCN: moderation 保留了名词「尺度」的含义。

items.example: Moderate prices suit most families.
items.exampleCN: 适中的价格适合大多数家庭。

items.example: The suffix -or forms moderator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 moderator。

items.meaning: a person who holds the limits
items.example: The moderator removed the rude posts.
items.exampleCN: 审核员删除了无礼的帖子。

items.example: Im- plus moderate gives immoderate.
items.exampleCN: im- 加 moderate 构成 immoderate。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms moderately.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 moderately。

latinEntries.exampleCN: modus 也衍生出英语 mode。
moderari 是 moderate 的前身。

latinEntries.example: Moderatio is the direct Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: moderatio 是直接的拉丁语来源。

latinEntries.example: Modestus is a close Latin cousin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: modestus 是关系很近的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 时髦的；赶时髦的；时尚的
definition_en: fashionable in a way that follows the latest style, often too keenly
core_image: 橱窗里的模特换上了本季最新款，路人都回头多看几眼
scene: 朋友劝他别买那台只是看起来时兴的新款小家电。His friends warned him not to waste money on a modish gadget that only looked smart for a few months.
sceneCN: 这里 modish 是「赶时髦的、时兴的」（第 1 个义项：紧跟当下潮流，常含追赶之意）；句意：他的朋友劝他别把钱浪费在一台只有几个月显得时髦的小家电上。

pos.zh: 时髦的；赶时髦的；时兴的

derivatives.zh: modish 的基础名词，由拉丁语 modus 而来，义为「方式；流行式样」
由 modish 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「时髦地」
由 modish 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「时髦；赶时髦的风气」
与 mode 同源的旧式名词，义为「女装设计师」，今多用于历史语境

senses.title: Fashionable and in tune with the latest style
senses.definition: following the newest fashion, especially in clothes, homes, or speech
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟最新时尚的，尤指衣着、家居或措辞方面
senses.example: She bought a modish little hat for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 她为婚礼买了一顶时髦的小帽子。
senses.why: Mode means fashion as well as manner, and adding -ish gives the adjective of being in that mode, so the word simply says that something follows the current mode.
senses.whyCN: mode 既可指方式，也可指风尚；加上 -ish 就成了「处于这一风尚之中」的形容词，所以这个词直接说明某物正跟着当下的风尚走。

senses.title: Keenly, even too eagerly, fashionable
senses.definition: so eager to be fashionable that the effort itself is noticeable
senses.definitionCN: 过于急于显得时尚，以至于能看出刻意经营的痕迹
senses.example: The essay is full of modish jargon that will date quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章满是赶潮流的术语，过不了多久就会过时。
senses.why: The suffix -ish often carries a slight hint of excess, so the same adjective also marks the person or idea that chases a style too hard.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ish 常带一点「过分」的暗示，因此同一个形容词也被用来指那种过分追逐某种风气的人或想法。

senses.title: Belonging to a particular manner or mode
senses.titleCN: 符合某种方式的；循例的
senses.definition: following a set manner or style that belongs to a given period or group
senses.definitionCN: 遵循某一时期或某一群体固定方式与风格的
senses.example: The painter stayed with a modish idiom of the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家一直沿用那个十年里流行的创作语汇。
senses.why: Before the word meant stylish, mode carried the neutral sense of manner, and the adjective keeps that older, more neutral reading.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「时髦」之前，mode 本就有中性的「方式」之义，形容词也保留了这个更早、更中性的义项。

intro.en: Modish is formed in English from mode plus the adjective suffix -ish, and mode itself goes back to Latin modus, a measure or manner.
intro.cn: modish 是在英语内部由 mode 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成的，而 mode 本身源于拉丁语 modus（尺度、方式）。

items.en: Modus means a measure, a manner, or a way.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、方式或途径。

items.en: Mode carries the sense of manner and fashion into French.
items.cn: mode 在法语中带有「方式」与「风尚」之义。

items.en: Mode enters English as a word for manner and for current fashion.
items.cn: mode 进入英语，既指方式，也指当下的风尚。

items.en: Mode plus -ish gives modish, meaning in the current fashion.
items.cn: mode 加 -ish 构成 modish，义为「合乎当下风尚的」。

items.en: Modish becomes a mildly critical word for whatever is merely trendy.
items.cn: modish 逐渐带有轻微的批评意味，指「只是跟风赶潮流」的东西。

items.en: Modish now appears mostly in reviews and commentary about style.
items.cn: 现代英语中 modish 多出现在关于风格的评论与议论文字里。

note.en: Modish is the -ish adjective of mode, and it stands close to fashionable, trendy, and stylish with a slightly critical tone.
note.cn: modish 是 mode 的 -ish 形容词，与 fashionable、trendy、stylish 意义相近，但略带批评意味。

entries.definition: a way of doing something, or a current fashion
entries.definitionCN: 方式；风尚（modish 的基础名词）

entries.definition: the quality of being modish
entries.definitionCN: 时髦；赶时髦的品质（modish 加 -ness 构成）

entries.definition: in a fashionable manner
entries.definitionCN: 时髦地（modish 加 -ly 构成）

entries.definition: wearing or using what is popular now
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的；流行的，中性而常用

entries.definition: very fashionable in a slightly disapproving way
entries.definitionCN: 口语法，指「很时髦」，同样带一点贬义

entries.definition: attractive and well designed
entries.definitionCN: 有型的；漂亮的，多为褒义，不带追逐之意

normalIntro.en: Modish is mode with -ish on the end: whatever is in the current mode, and often a little too eager to be so.
normalIntro.cn: modish 就是 mode 后面加上 -ish：凡是正处于当下风尚之中的东西，而且常常显得过于急于如此。

normal.en: Mode means the current fashion, so modish describes things that wear it.
normal.cn: mode 指当下的风尚，modish 就形容正在穿用它的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ish means having the qualities of, as in childish and stylish.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ish 表示「具有……的特性」，如 childish 与 stylish。

normal.en: Modish clothes are worn by people who follow every new season.
normal.cn: modish clothes 指每季新款都要跟、都要穿的那些人身上的衣服。

normal.en: Modishly is the adverb, modishness the noun of being trendy.
normal.cn: modishly 是副词，modishness 是「赶时髦」这一性质的名词。

normal.en: In reviews, modish often hints that the fashion will not last.
normal.cn: 在评论文字里，modish 常常暗示这股风尚不会长久。

abstract.en: Picture a mannequin dressed in this season only.
abstract.cn: 想象一个模特只穿本季的衣服。

abstract.en: Imagine a student using a polished new term precisely because it is new.
abstract.cn: 想象一名学生专门挑了一个时髦的新词来用，只因它新鲜。

abstract.en: See a pair of shoes with a label that announces the year it was made.
abstract.cn: 想象一双鞋的标签上直接印着生产年份，以显示出道时间。

examples.en: The shop sells modish bags at rather high prices.
examples.cn: 这家店以很高的价格出售时髦的手袋。

examples.en: Her modish style made her stand out in the office.
examples.cn: 她时髦的打扮让她在办公室里很显眼。

examples.en: Critics call the plan a modish slogan with no detail.
examples.cn: 批评者称这个计划不过是赶潮流的口号，没有任何细节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「末的」——时尚走到末尾的那一阵，就是赶时髦；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度；方式）→ 古法语 mode（方式；风尚）→ 英语 mode + 形容词后缀 -ish → modish，核心义「正处于当下风尚之中」。

sensesIntro.en: Modish starts with the neutral idea of matching the current mode, becomes the everyday adjective for fashionable things, and then takes on a critical edge for those who chase a style too eagerly.
sensesIntro.cn: modish 起于「与当下风尚相符」这一中性观念，成为形容时髦之物的日常形容词，随后又带上批评色彩，专指过分追逐某种风气的人或想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop window dressed in this season only.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇只按本季最新款布置的橱窗。

branches.en: Following the newest fashion is the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 紧跟最新时尚，是这个词最日常的义项。

branches.en: The same adjective turns critical when the effort to follow is visible.
branches.cn: 当追逐的痕迹明显时，同一个形容词就带上批评意味。

branches.en: The older neutral sense of mode as manner still lives in the adjective.
branches.cn: mode 表示「方式」的古老中性义，仍保留在这个形容词里。

branches.en: Both senses describe people who follow the fashion, but the second judges them.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述跟随风尚的人，只是第二个义项是在作出评价。

branches.en: Matching a period manner and matching a current mode share the idea of conformity.
branches.cn: 符合某一时期的做法与符合当下风尚，共享「顺应」这一观念。

intro.en: Modish is mode plus the adjective suffix -ish, with other relatives formed by -ly, -ness, and the older form modiste.
intro.cn: modish 由 mode 加形容词后缀 -ish 构成，另由 -ly、-ness 以及旧式形式 modiste 构成相关词。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus means a measure or manner, and modus is behind mode, which in turn grows modish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus 意为尺度或方式，modus 衍生出 mode，mode 再构成 modish。

items.example: Modus is the deepest source of the family.
items.exampleCN: modus 是这个词族最深的来源。

items.meaning: a way, or a current fashion
items.example: Mode is the base of modish.
items.exampleCN: mode 是 modish 的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ish turns mode into modish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 把 mode 变成 modish。

items.example: Modish describes anything in vogue.
items.exampleCN: modish 形容一切正流行的事物。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms modishly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 modishly。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms modishness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 modishness。

items.meaningCN: 女装设计师；做时髦服装的人
items.example: Modiste shares the fashion sense of mode.
items.exampleCN: modiste 与 mode 共享「风尚」这一层含义。

items.example: Outmoded is the opposite pole of modish.
items.exampleCN: outmoded 是 modish 的对立面。

items.example: Modishness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: modishness 指「时髦」这一性质本身。

items.example: Modishly describes how someone dresses.
items.exampleCN: modishly 描述某人穿着的方式。

latinEntries.example: Modus gives English mode and modish.
latinEntries.exampleCN: modus 衍生出英语 mode 与 modish。

latinEntries.example: Modicus is a Latin cousin of modus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: modicus 是 modus 的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 单元；模块；（课程或软件的）单元；组件；（航天器）舱；模（数学）
definition_en: one of several separate units that can be combined to build a larger structure, course, system or spacecraft
core_image: 一座小尺子的度量，被当作可以重复拼起来的积木单元
scene: 大学建筑系的选课表上，同一个单元既可单独选修，也能拼成整套课程。Students can take each module on its own or combine them into a full degree.
sceneCN: 这里 module 是「课程单元」（第 1 个义项：可独立选择、又能组合成整体的单元）；句意：学生可以单独选修每个单元，也可以把它们组合成完整学位。图中可辨识物件：选课表、方块积木、量尺。

pos.zh: 模块；单元；组件；（课程或软件的）单元；（航天器）舱

derivatives.zh: 由 module 加形容词后缀 -ar 构成，义为「模块化的；组合式的」
由 modular 加 -ity 构成，义为「模块化程度；可组合性」
由 modular 加 -ize 构成，义为「模块化；把……拆成模块」
与 module 同出拉丁语 modus（尺度），指「模数；模量」

senses.title: One unit of a course
senses.definition: one of the separate units into which a course or study programme is divided
senses.definitionCN: 课程或学习项目被划分成的独立单元之一
senses.example: The first module covers basic statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个单元讲基础统计学。
senses.why: A course was once measured out in fixed portions, and each portion was one measure of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 课程本来就是按固定份量切分的，每一份就是整体的一个「度量单位」。

senses.title: A self-contained part of a design
senses.definition: a part of a system, building, or machine that is built and fitted separately and can be combined with others
senses.definitionCN: 系统、建筑或机器中单独制造并安装、可与其他部分组合的部件
senses.example: The kitchen module can be fitted on either side of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 这个厨房模块可装在房间任一侧。
senses.why: If a thing is a measure, it can be repeated: identical measures stack together into a larger structure.
senses.whyCN: 既然一件东西是一个度量单位，它就可以重复：相同的单位堆叠起来，组成更大的结构。

senses.title: A separate unit in software
senses.definition: a unit of a computer program that is developed and tested on its own and then linked with other units
senses.definitionCN: 计算机程序中单独开发、测试，再与其他单元连接的程序单元
senses.example: The login module is tested before it is added to the app.
senses.exampleCN: 登录模块在加入应用之前先经过测试。
senses.why: Software borrowed the architectural module: one part built to a fixed interface so that whole systems can be assembled from it.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用了建筑的模块概念：按固定接口造好一个部件，整套系统就能用它拼装起来。

senses.title: A section of a spacecraft
senses.definition: a self-contained section of a spacecraft or space station that has its own function
senses.definitionCN: 航天器或空间站中具有独立功能的舱段
senses.example: The lunar module separated from the command ship above the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 登月舱在月球上空与指令舱分离。
senses.why: Spacecraft are built and checked as modules, each sealed unit a measure that can be docked to the next.
senses.whyCN: 航天器是按模块分段建造和检查的，每个封闭单元都是一个可与下一段对接的度量单位。

senses.title: A modulus in mathematics
senses.definition: a fixed quantity that serves as a unit of measurement or of regular repetition, as in modular arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 作为测量或规律重复基准的固定量，如模运算中的模
senses.example: In modular arithmetic, numbers wrap around at a fixed modulus.
senses.exampleCN: 在模运算中，数字在固定的模数处折返。
senses.why: This is the Latin sense at its most literal: modulus was the little measure kept for the next standard.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语含义最字面的一面：modulus 就是留着用来对照下一个标准的「小尺度」。

intro.en: Module is a small Latin noun for a measure, which English took through French and then applied to courses, machines, software and spacecraft.
intro.cn: module 是拉丁语中表示「尺度」的小词，英语经法语借入后，逐步用到课程、机器、软件与航天器上。

items.en: Modus meant measure, manner or way, and it also stands behind mode, model and modern.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、方式、样式」，它也是 mode、model、modern 的来源。

items.en: The diminutive modulus meant a small measure or a standard. Its first written dates are uncertain, but it is attested in Roman technical writing.
items.cn: 指小形式 modulus 意为「小尺度、标准量」。确切首见年代不确定，但罗马技术文献中已有使用。

items.en: French took the word as a technical term for a fixed measure in building and later in mathematics.
items.cn: 法语把它用作建筑中固定尺度的术语，后来又用于数学。

items.en: English takes module in the sixteenth century, first in the mathematical sense of a constant measure.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 module，最早用于表示常数的数学义。

items.en: Twentieth-century design and computing turn the fixed measure into a self-contained unit that can be repeated and combined.
items.cn: 二十世纪的设计与计算机领域把「固定尺度」变成可重复、可组合的独立单元。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the Latin root modus, meaning measure; the near-meaning group gathers other words for separable parts with different images.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词根 modus（尺度）生出的一族词；近义组收其他表示「可分离部件」的词，它们的意象各不相同。

entries.definition: made from separate units that can be combined or replaced
entries.definitionCN: 由可组合、可替换的独立单元构成的

entries.definition: a way of doing something or a particular setting of a device
entries.definitionCN: 方式；模式；设备的某种设定

entries.definition: a constant measure used as a standard in mathematics or physics
entries.definitionCN: 数学或物理中作为基准的常数量

entries.definition: to vary sound, signal or feeling within measured limits
entries.definitionCN: 在限定的尺寸内调节声音、信号或情绪

entries.definition: a single complete thing or the least part of a larger whole
entries.definitionCN: 一个完整单位，或整体中最小的部分

entries.definition: a part of a machine or system, seen in relation to the whole it fits into
entries.definitionCN: 机器或系统的部件，强调它与整体的配合

entries.definition: a solid piece, often rectangular, that is stacked with others in building
entries.definitionCN: 常为方形的块体，在建造中与其他块体堆叠

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin root modus and the real phrases that module appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁词根 modus，以及 module 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Modus means measure; a module is one measure that can be repeated.
normal.cn: modus 是「尺度」；module 就是可以重复使用的度量单位。

normal.en: The same root gives mode, model and modern, all built on the idea of manner or measure.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 mode、model、modern，它们都建立在「方式、尺度」的观念上。

normal.en: Modular means built from modules, so the adjective and the noun travel together.
normal.cn: modular 意为「由模块构成的」，这个形容词和名词是一体的。

normal.en: A course is taught in modules, so a module is never the whole degree.
normal.cn: 课程是按模块讲授的，所以一个 module 从来不是完整的学位。

normal.en: The lunar module is the sealed unit that detaches and lands.
normal.cn: lunar module 就是那个可以分离并着陆的封闭单元。

abstract.en: Picture a small ruler held next to a long wall: the ruler is the one measure that tells you the size of everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小尺子贴在长墙边：这把尺子就是丈量一切的度量单位。

abstract.en: Picture identical boxes snapping together, each one able to leave the pile and stand alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一模一样的盒子扣在一起，每个都能单独抽出来独立站立。

abstract.en: Picture a program assembled like a rack of cards, one card for login, one for payment.
abstract.cn: 想象一个程序像一叠插件卡拼成，一张管登录，一张管支付。

examples.en: Each module of the course ends with a short written test.
examples.cn: 课程的每个单元都以一次简短的笔试结束。

examples.en: The engineers replaced the damaged module in less than an hour.
examples.cn: 工程师在不到一小时内更换了受损的模块。

examples.en: Teachers praised the new module on climate change.
examples.cn: 教师们称赞了关于气候变化的新模块。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸dule」——摸一下尺子，量一个格子：一个模块、一个单元。这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 modus「尺度、方式、样式」→ 指小形式 modulus「小尺度、标准量」→ 法语技术用语 module「建筑中的固定尺度」→ 英语 module「度量；模；模块」。核心义「可重复的度量单位」。

sensesIntro.en: Module begins as a fixed measure, then grows into any self-contained unit that can be repeated and combined: a study unit, a machine part, a code unit, a spacecraft section and a modulus.
sensesIntro.cn: module 起初是固定的度量，后来扩展为任何可重复、可组合的独立单元：课程单元、机器部件、代码单元、航天器舱段与数学上的模。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small ruler is kept beside longer building blocks so that each block is one fixed measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小把尺子守在长长的积木旁，每块积木都是一个固定的度量。

branches.en: SCHOOL: a course is divided into fixed portions, and each portion is one measure.
branches.cn: 学校线：课程被切成固定份量，每一份就是一个度量。

branches.en: BUILDING: the measure becomes a part that is manufactured separately and fitted with others.
branches.cn: 建筑线：度量变成单独制造、再与其他部件装配的部件。

branches.en: CODE: software takes the same building block and gives it a programming interface.
branches.cn: 代码线：软件借来同样的积木，只是给它一个编程接口。

branches.en: SPACE: a sealed section of a spacecraft is a module that detaches and docks.
branches.cn: 太空线：航天器里的封闭舱段是可分离、可对接的模块。

branches.en: The oldest and the newest meet: modulus is the measure itself, while the latest modules are units built to repeat it.
branches.cn: 最早与最新相接：modulus 是度量本身，而最新的模块是按它重复造出的单元。

intro.en: Module rests on the Latin root mod- for measure, and English builds modular, modularity and modularize around it.
intro.cn: module 建立在拉丁语表示「尺度」的词根 mod- 上，英语围绕它构成 modular、modularity 与 modularize。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus, modulus and the verb modulari are all recorded, so only the Indo-European background is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus、modulus 与动词 modulari 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧语背景属于重构。

items.example: The root mod- carries the idea of measuring.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mod- 带有「衡量」的意思。

items.example: Modus is the measure noun behind mode and model.
items.exampleCN: modus 是 mode 与 model 背后的名词。

items.example: The diminutive means a little measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个指小名词意为「小小的尺度」。

items.example: The suffix -ule marks something small.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ule 表示「小」。

items.meaning: a separate unit that can be combined
items.meaningCN: 可与其他部分组合的独立单元
items.example: Module is the direct English continuation.
items.exampleCN: module 是直接延续到英语的形式。

items.example: It forms modular from module.
items.exampleCN: 它由 module 构成 modular。

items.meaning: the quality of being built from modules
items.example: Modularity was the goal of the design team.
items.exampleCN: 模块化是设计团队的目标。

items.example: They decided to modularize the old system.
items.exampleCN: 他们决定把旧系统模块化。

items.example: Mode keeps the Latin sense of manner.
items.exampleCN: mode 保留了拉丁语「方式」的含义。

items.example: It forms modularity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 modularity。

latinEntries.meaning: to measure, to set to a rhythm

definition_zh: 使湿润；弄湿；沾湿；变湿；（眼睛）变得湿润
definition_en: to make something slightly wet, or to become slightly wet
core_image: 指尖蘸一点水，轻轻抹在干面包或干纸张的表面
scene: 烤面包出炉后太干，老人用手指蘸水沿边缘抹了一圈。Grandma moistened the edges of the pastry before sealing it.
sceneCN: 这里 moisten 是「使湿润」（第 1 个义项：让某物表面略带水分）；句意：奶奶在封口前把面皮边缘弄湿。图中可辨识物件：烤盘、面粉、一杯水。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词源：义为「湿润的；微湿的」
与 moist 同源，义为「湿气；水分；水分含量」
由 moist 加 -ness 构成，义为「湿气；湿润状态」
由 moisture 加 -ize 构成，义为「给皮肤补水；保湿」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「润湿的过程」

senses.title: To make something slightly wet
senses.definition: to put a small amount of water or liquid on something so that it becomes slightly wet
senses.definitionCN: 在某物上施少量水或液体，使其变得微湿
senses.example: Moisten the paper with a damp cloth and it will lie flat.
senses.exampleCN: 用湿布把纸弄湿，它就会平贴。
senses.why: The verb was made from the adjective moist plus -en, so it simply names the act of bringing about that damp quality.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由形容词 moist 加 -en 构成，所以它只是给「变得湿润」这个性质命名了动作。

senses.title: To become slightly wet
senses.definition: to become slightly wet, especially of lips, eyes or a surface
senses.definitionCN: 变得微湿，尤指嘴唇、眼睛或某表面
senses.example: Her eyes moistened as the choir began to sing.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团一开始唱，她的眼睛就湿润了。
senses.why: Many -en verbs work both ways, so the same form lets the thing itself take on the slight wetness.
senses.whyCN: 许多 -en 动词都可以双向使用，因此同一个形式也能表示事物本身染上那一点湿意。

senses.title: To wet something so it works
senses.definition: to apply a little liquid to a surface so that something seals, sticks or works properly
senses.definitionCN: 给表面抹一点液体，使某物能密封、粘贴或正常起作用
senses.example: Moisten the stamp before pressing it onto the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 把邮票沾湿，再按到信封上。
senses.why: This is the practical side of the image: the small amount of water is not decorative but makes the join hold.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象的实用面：那一点水不是为了好看，而是让接合处粘得住。

senses.title: To keep plant soil damp
senses.definition: to add water to soil or compost in small amounts so that seeds and roots can grow
senses.definitionCN: 向土壤或培养土少量加水，供种子与根系生长
senses.example: Moisten the compost before you sow the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 播种前先把培养土润湿。
senses.why: Gardening uses the same gentle degree of wetness: enough for life, never a flood.
senses.whyCN: 园艺用的是同样的「轻微湿度」：够生命需要，但绝不浇成一片水涝。

intro.en: Moisten is a native English formation from the adjective moist and the verb-forming suffix -en; the deep background of moist is debated and is marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: moisten 是英语本土构词：由形容词 moist 加动词后缀 -en 构成；moist 的更早来源有争议，本文标注为不确定。

items.en: Old French moiste meant wet, damp or fresh, and also newly made or still soft.
items.cn: 古法语 moiste 意为「湿的、潮湿的、新鲜的」，也有「刚做成、仍柔软」的意思。

items.en: English adopts moiste as moist, used for damp air, damp earth and food that has not dried out.
items.cn: 英语借入 moiste 成为 moist，用于潮湿的空气、湿润的土地和未变干的食物。

items.en: A common reconstruction is Vulgar Latin *muscidus, meaning mouldy, altered from Latin mucidus. This step is a hypothesis, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 常见一种重构：俗拉丁语 *muscidus「发霉的」，是拉丁语 mucidus 的变形。这一步属于假说，并无文献记录。

items.en: Other scholars link the family to Latin madidus, meaning wet, and madere, to be wet. The two hypotheses are usually listed side by side.
items.cn: 另一些学者把这一词族联系到拉丁语 madidus「湿透的」与 madere「潮湿」。两种假说通常并列陈述。

items.en: The verb moisten is formed in English from moist plus -en, following other -en verbs of the same period.
items.cn: 动词 moisten 在英语中由 moist 加 -en 构成，与同时期其他 -en 动词的构词方式相同。

items.en: Cooking, gardening, printing and medicine all adopt the verb for controlling small amounts of moisture.
items.cn: 烹饪、园艺、印刷与医学都采用这个词，用来控制少量的水分。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the moist family and verbs built with -en; the near-meaning group gathers other words for making something wet, at different degrees.
note.cn: 形近组收 moist 词族的词以及用 -en 构词的动词；近义组收其他表示「弄湿」的词，湿度强弱各不相同。

entries.definition: slightly wet, often in a way that is pleasant or intended
entries.definitionCN: 微湿的，常是令人舒服或有意为之的湿度

entries.definition: small amounts of water present in air or in a substance
entries.definitionCN: 空气中或物质里含有的少量水分

entries.definition: a cream that adds water to the skin
entries.definitionCN: 给皮肤补充水分的护肤品

entries.definition: a mint cocktail; it only looks similar and comes from another root
entries.definitionCN: 薄荷鸡尾酒；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to make slightly wet, or to make a feeling less strong
entries.definitionCN: 使微湿；也可指减弱某种情绪

entries.definition: to cover with water; stronger than moisten
entries.definitionCN: 把某物弄湿；程度比 moisten 更强

entries.definition: to leave something in liquid until it is completely wet
entries.definitionCN: 把某物浸在液体中直到完全湿透

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real word family of moist and the -en verb pattern that moisten belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 moist 的真实词族，以及 moisten 所属的 -en 动词构词规律。

normal.en: moist plus -en makes a verb, just as wide plus -en makes widen.
normal.cn: moist 加 -en 变成动词，就像 wide 加 -en 变成 widen。

normal.en: The family runs moist, moisten, moisture and moisturise, all about a little water.
normal.cn: 这个词族是 moist、moisten、moisture、moisturise，全都在说「一点点水」。

normal.en: Cooks moisten pastry edges with water so that the join seals.
normal.cn: 厨师用水弄湿面皮边缘，让接缝粘牢。

normal.en: The word keeps the light degree of wetness: damp, not soaking.
normal.cn: 这个词保持「轻微湿度」的度量：是微湿，不是湿透。

normal.en: Eyes that moisten are wet with tears, a soft and literal use.
normal.cn: moisten 的眼睛就是被泪水润湿，这是温和而字面的用法。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip touched to a glass of water, then drawn along the edge of a pie crust.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖碰一下水杯，再沿馅饼皮边缘抹过去。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp flipped face up, one breath of water, and it sticks.
abstract.cn: 想象邮票翻面朝上，沾一点水，就贴住了。

abstract.en: Picture dry soil darkening as a few drops fall, just enough for a seed.
abstract.cn: 想象干土滴上几滴水而变深色，刚好够一颗种子发芽。

examples.en: She moistened a cloth and wiped the dusty table.
examples.cn: 她把布沾湿，擦了擦满是灰尘的桌子。

examples.en: The gardener moistens the seedlings every morning.
examples.cn: 园丁每天早上给幼苗浇些水。

examples.en: His mouth felt dry, so he moistened his lips with tea.
examples.cn: 他嘴干了，用茶润了润嘴唇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫伊斯」——莫让伊斯太干，蘸一点水：使湿润。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 moiste「湿的、新鲜的」→ 中古英语 moist；英语再以 moist + 动词后缀 -en（同类如 widen、deepen）构成 moisten「使湿润」。moist 的拉丁语背景有两种假说：俗拉丁语重构形式 *muscidus（发霉的）或拉丁语 madidus/madere（湿的），尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Moisten is one action of adding a little water, seen as making a surface damp, as becoming damp itself, as a practical step before sealing, and as the gardener feeding soil.
sensesIntro.cn: moisten 是「加一点水」这同一个动作：让表面微湿、自身变湿、封口前的实用一步，以及园丁给土壤补水。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip carries one drop of water and draws it softly along a dry edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖沾着一滴水，沿干燥的边缘轻轻抹过。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the verb names the person who brings the dampness onto something.
branches.cn: 施事线：动词指那个把湿意加到某物上的人。

branches.en: THE CHANGE: with the same -en pattern, the subject itself takes on the dampness.
branches.cn: 变化线：按同样的 -en 规律，主语本身染上了湿意。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL STEP: the water is there to make a seal, not for its own sake.
branches.cn: 实用线：那点水是为了粘合密封，并非只为了好看。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the same small measure of water keeps soil and seed alive.
branches.cn: 园艺线：同样少量的水维持着土壤与种子的生命。

branches.en: Both directions share the core image: the dampness is always slight, never a flood.
branches.cn: 两个方向共享同一核心意象：湿意始终轻微，不会成涝。

intro.en: Moisten is a home-made English verb: an adjective of Old French origin plus a native -en suffix, with the moist family around it.
intro.cn: moisten 是英语本土造的动词：一个源自法语的形容词加上本土词尾 -en，周围是 moist 一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin madidus and madere are recorded forms that one hypothesis links to moist; the other hypothesis uses a reconstructed Vulgar Latin *muscidus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 madidus 与 madere 是有记录的实词，一种假说把它们与 moist 联系起来；另一种假说则使用重构的俗拉丁语 *muscidus。

items.example: Moist is the adjective the verb is built on.
items.exampleCN: moist 是构成这个动词的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -en turns an adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Moisten follows the same path as deepen.
items.exampleCN: moisten 与 deepen 走的是同一条构词路径。

items.example: Moisture is the noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: moisture 是这一族的抽象名词。

items.example: The -ness suffix forms moistness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 moistness。

items.meaning: to add moisture to the skin
items.example: The suffix -ize forms moisturize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 moisturize。

items.example: Deepen shows the same suffix at work.
items.exampleCN: deepen 展示了同一个后缀的用法。

items.example: Dampen is a close neighbour of moisten.
items.exampleCN: dampen 是 moisten 的近邻。

items.example: One hypothesis links madere to the moist family.
items.exampleCN: 有一种假说把 madere 与 moist 词族联系起来。

definition_zh: 重大的；重要的；影响深远的；（决定）非同小可的
definition_en: very important or serious, especially because it has great and lasting effects
core_image: 天平的一端突然沉下去：一件决定的分量重得压住了另一端
scene: 会议室里，所有人盯着桌上那份决定公司命运的合同，迟迟没人先开口。Everyone in the room knew that this momentous decision would change the small town forever.
sceneCN: 这里 momentous 是「重大的」（第 1 个义项：影响深远的重要事件或决定）；句意：房间里的每个人都明白，这个重大的决定将永远改变这座小镇。图中可辨识物件：合同、天平、旧挂钟。

pos.zh: 形容词：重大的；重要的；影响深远的

derivatives.zh: 本词的核心来源：拉丁语「运动、推动力」，英语义为「时刻」
与 moment 同出拉丁语 momentum，义为「动量；势头」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「重大性；重要性」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「重大地；举足轻重地」
由 moment 加 -ary 与 -ly 构成，义为「片刻地；转眼之间」

senses.title: Of great importance
senses.definition: extremely important or serious, especially because of the lasting effects it will have
senses.definitionCN: 极其重要或严重，尤指会带来持久影响
senses.example: The signing of the treaty was a momentous occasion for both nations.
senses.exampleCN: 条约的签署对两国都是重大时刻。
senses.why: Latin momentum was the weight of a moving body, so a momentous matter is one heavy enough to move the course of events.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 momentum 指运动物体的重量，所以 momentous 的事情就是重到足以推动事件走向的事情。

senses.title: Setting a decisive turning point
senses.definition: marking a turning point after which a situation will never be the same
senses.definitionCN: 标志转折点，此后形势将不再一样
senses.example: Her election was a momentous step for the village.
senses.exampleCN: 她的当选对这个村庄是决定性的转折。
senses.why: Something with enough momentum carries the present forward into a new state, so a momentous choice is one that tips the balance.
senses.whyCN: 动量足够大的东西会把现在带进新的状态，所以 momentous 的选择就是打破平衡的那一下。

senses.title: Pompous in tone, used for small matters
senses.titleCN: 小题大做的；措辞隆重的
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way for an event that is being treated as far more important than it is
senses.definitionCN: 带轻微调侃意味，指被当成远比实际重要的事
senses.example: The club called its new kettle a momentous invention.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部把新水壶称作一项重大发明。
senses.why: Once the word marks real historical weight, giving it to something tiny makes the mismatch itself the joke.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用来标记真实的历史分量，把它用在极小的事上，这种落差本身就构成了笑点。

intro.en: Momentous means full of moment, and Latin momentum goes back to the verb movere, to move: the weight and push of a moving body.
intro.cn: momentous 字面义是「充满 moment」，而拉丁语 momentum 源于动词 movere（推动），指运动物体的重量与冲力。

items.en: The verb movere belongs to a root commonly reconstructed as *mew-, to push away. The deeper background of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 movere 属于一个通常重构为 *mew-（推开）的词根。这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Movere means to move or set in motion, and its family includes momentum.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使运动」，这一族包括 momentum 等词。

items.en: Momentum meant a movement, the change in a balance, and the weight that decides which way a scale tips.
items.cn: momentum 意为「运动」、天平的摆动，以及决定天平倒向哪一边的重量。

items.en: The English noun moment comes in through Old French and splits into a point in time and an important factor.
items.cn: 英语名词 moment 经古法语进入，分出「时间的一点」与「重要因素」两条线。

items.en: The adjective momentous forms on moment plus the suffix -ous, with the sense of something of great weight or consequence.
items.cn: 形容词 momentous 由 moment 加后缀 -ous 构成，表示有重大分量、后果严重的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on Latin movere and on the moment family; the near-meaning group gathers other words for what matters, with different intensity and tone.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 movere 与 moment 一族词；近义组收其他表示「重要」的词，强度与语气各不相同。

entries.definition: a very short period of time, or a particular point when something happens
entries.definitionCN: 片刻，或某事发生的某一时刻

entries.definition: the force of a body in motion, or the growing strength of a process
entries.definitionCN: 运动物体的动量，或某进程不断累积的势头

entries.definition: an act of moving, or a group working for a shared aim
entries.definitionCN: 移动的动作，或为共同目标行动的一群人

entries.definition: lasting only for a very short time
entries.definitionCN: 只持续极短时间的。它和 momentous 拼写相近，意思却完全相反。

entries.definition: important enough to be noticed or to change something
entries.definitionCN: 重要到值得注意或能带来改变的

entries.definition: important in history and likely to be long remembered
entries.definitionCN: 在历史上有重要性、容易被长久记住的

entries.definition: extremely important because of what depends on it
entries.definitionCN: 因后果全系于此而极其关键的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root of momentum and the phrases that momentous appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 momentum 的真实拉丁词根，以及 momentous 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Moment plus -ous means full of moment: an event with real weight.
normal.cn: moment 加 -ous 意为「充满 moment」：一个有真实分量的时刻。

normal.en: The Latin root is movere, to move, so weight and motion belong together.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是 movere（推动），所以「重量」与「运动」连在一起。

normal.en: Momentous collocates with decision, occasion, change and event, never with a minor detail.
normal.cn: momentous 常与 decision、occasion、change、event 搭配，从不用在细枝末节上。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with momentary: one lasts forever in memory, the other a second.
normal.cn: 不要与 momentary 混淆：一个留在记忆里很久，一个只持续一瞬。

normal.en: Momentous decisions are the ones historians later retell.
normal.cn: momentous 的决定，就是日后历史学家会反复讲述的那些。

abstract.en: Picture a huge iron weight dropped onto one pan of a scale: the beam slams down.
abstract.cn: 想象一块大铁块落在天平一端：横梁猛地压下去。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone rolled from a hilltop; it grows heavier and faster and nothing can stop it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石子从山顶滚下，越滚越重越快，什么也挡不住。

abstract.en: Picture a birthday cake announced as a momentous event: the grand word and the tiny cake do not fit.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把生日蛋糕宣布为重大事件：盛大的词与小小的蛋糕并不相配。

examples.en: Choosing a university is a momentous decision for a teenager.
examples.cn: 对青少年而言，选择大学是一个重大的决定。

examples.en: The fall of the wall was a momentous event in European history.
examples.cn: 柏林墙的倒塌是欧洲历史上的重大事件。

examples.en: The council described the new bus timetable as momentous, which made everyone laugh.
examples.cn: 委员会把新的公交时刻表称为「重大事件」，把大家都逗笑了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸门特斯」——摸着门框退一步，说这是重大时刻：重大的。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 movere「推动、移动」→ momentum「运动；天平摆动的重量」→ moment（经古法语 moment「时刻、片刻」）→ 英语 momentous「有分量的、重大的」。核心义「沉重到能推动局势」。词根更早的印欧语重构形式属于推定，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Momentous carries one idea through three uses: something so heavy with consequence that it turns the course of events, then a clear turning point, and finally a mocking label for small things.
sensesIntro.cn: momentous 把一个观念贯穿三种用法：重到能扭转局势的事，明确的转折点，最后是对小事略带调侃的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy weight falls on one side of a scale and the beam cannot stay level.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉重的重量压在天平一端，横梁再也无法保持水平。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: an important event is one that carries real weight of consequence.
branches.cn: 重量线：重要的事件就是真正带有后果分量的事件。

branches.en: THE TURN: once the scale tips, the situation moves into a new state that cannot be reversed.
branches.cn: 转折线：天平一旦倾倒，局面就进入无法回头的新状态。

branches.en: THE JOKE: using the grand word for small things lets the mismatch carry the humour.
branches.cn: 调侃线：把宏大的词用在小事上，落差本身就成了笑点。

branches.en: A momentous decision is both heavy with consequence and the point that tips the balance.
branches.cn: 一个 momentous 的决定既后果沉重，又是让天平倾倒的那一刻。

branches.en: The stronger the word is in its serious sense, the sharper its mocking use becomes.
branches.cn: 这个词在严肃义上越有分量，它带调侃的用法就越尖锐。

intro.en: Momentous is the adjective of moment, and the whole family reaches back through Latin momentum to the verb movere, to move.
intro.cn: momentous 是 moment 的形容词，整个词族经拉丁语 momentum 追溯到动词 movere（推动）。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere, momentum and the noun moment are all recorded; only the Indo-European root of movere is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere、momentum 与名词 moment 均有文献记录，只有 movere 的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The verb movere is the movement root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 动词 movere 是这一词族的「运动」词根。

items.meaning: movement, weight, the turn of a balance
items.example: Momentum is the source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: momentum 是英语名词的来源。

items.meaning: a point in time, or importance
items.example: Moment is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: moment 是这个形容词的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms momentous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 momentous。

items.example: Momentous describes events with lasting effect.
items.exampleCN: momentous 描述有持久影响的事件。

items.example: It forms momentousness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 momentousness。

items.example: The day began momentously at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 这一天在黎明时分以重大事件的姿态开始。

items.example: Momentarily means for a moment, not importantly.
items.exampleCN: momentarily 意为「片刻地」，与「重要」无关。

items.example: Momentary looks close but means the opposite of lasting weight.
items.exampleCN: momentary 外形相近，却与「持久分量」相反。

latinEntries.meaning: movement, weight of a moving body

definition_zh: 独石；整块巨石；巨型整体；铁板一块的庞大机构
definition_en: a single very large block of stone, or a huge organization that acts as one unchangeable whole
core_image: 荒原上一整块巨石直立着，没有接缝，推也推不动
scene: 考古队在平原上发现一整块竖立的巨大石块，周围没有别的建筑。The team found a huge monolith standing alone on the plain, with no other building near it.
sceneCN: 这里 monolith 是「整块巨石、独石」（第 1 个义项：单块巨石）；句意：考古队在平原上发现一块独自矗立的巨大独石，附近没有任何其他建筑。

pos.zh: 独石；整块巨石；庞然大物

collocations.zh: 推倒独石；撼动庞然大物

derivatives.zh: 由 monolith 加 -ic 构成的形容词，义为「整块巨石的；铁板一块的」
monolithic 加 -ly 构成的副词，义为「以铁板一块的方式」

senses.title: A single large block of stone
senses.definition: a very large piece of stone, especially one standing upright or carved as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 一整块巨大的石头，尤指竖立着或整体雕成者
senses.example: A granite monolith stands at the centre of the circle.
senses.exampleCN: 圆圈中央立着一块花岗岩独石。
senses.why: The Greek elements mean one plus stone, so the word names a rock that is one single piece rather than a built-up pile.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语两个成分分别是「一」和「石头」，所以这个词指一整块石头，而不是垒起来的石堆。

senses.title: A standing stone or statue
senses.definition: a monument, obelisk, or sculpture made from one block of stone
senses.definitionCN: 用一整块石头雕成的纪念碑、方尖碑或雕像
senses.example: The obelisk is a monolith cut from rose granite.
senses.exampleCN: 那方尖碑是用一整块玫瑰色花岗岩雕成的独石。
senses.why: Megalithic cultures often carved and moved one enormous stone as a monument, which fixed the word on obelisks, statues, and standing stones.
senses.whyCN: 巨石时代的文化常把一整块巨石雕琢、搬运来作纪念物，这就把该词固定在方尖碑、雕像和立石上。

senses.title: A huge single body or mass
senses.titleCN: 庞大而不可分割的整物
senses.definition: a massive object or mass that seems to be one solid whole
senses.definitionCN: 看起来是一整块、无法分割的巨大物体或体量
senses.example: From the road, the tower looks like a monolith of glass.
senses.exampleCN: 从公路上看，那座塔像一整块玻璃巨物。
senses.why: The image of one immovable stone extends to any object or building that reads as a single solid mass, such as concrete towers or airships.
senses.whyCN: 「一块推不动的石头」的意象延伸到任何看起来是一整块实体的物体，比如混凝土高楼或飞艇。

senses.title: A huge rigid organization
senses.definition: a very large organization or system that is slow, rigid, and hard to change
senses.definitionCN: 规模庞大、僵化、难以改变的组织或系统
senses.example: Critics call the ministry an unaccountable monolith.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个部委是一个问责困难的庞然大物。
senses.why: Sociology borrowed the stone for institutions that feel like one unbreakable mass, so the rock image becomes an image of rigidity and monopoly.
senses.whyCN: 社会学借这块石头形容像一整块无法敲碎的机构，于是石头意象变成了僵化与垄断的比喻。

senses.title: Computing: a single united program
senses.definition: in computing, a program or system built as one indivisible unit that is hard to split
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域指作为一个不可分割单元构建、难以拆分的程序或系统
senses.example: Moving from a monolith to smaller services took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 从单体架构切换到更小的服务，花了两年时间。
senses.why: The newest sense keeps the same idea: software that is one block of code behaves like a stone that cannot be prised apart.
senses.whyCN: 最新义项延续同一逻辑：一整块代码的软件就像撬不开的石头。

intro.en: Monolith comes from Greek monos, meaning single, and lithos, meaning stone; the Greek compound monolithos is attested, and English monolith appears in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: monolith 来自希腊语 monos（单一）与 lithos（石头）；希腊语复合词 monolithos 有文献可证，英语 monolith 于十九世纪出现。

items.en: Monos means alone or single, and lithos means stone.
items.cn: monos 意为独自、单一，lithos 意为石头。

items.en: Monolithos names an object cut from one single stone.
items.cn: monolithos 指用单独一块石头雕成的物体。

items.en: Latin writers use the borrowed form monolithus for statues made from one block.
items.cn: 拉丁语作者用借形 monolithus 指单块石头雕成的雕像。

items.en: English adopts monolith for obelisks, single-columns, and single-stone monuments.
items.cn: 英语采用 monolith 指方尖碑、单柱以及整石纪念物。

items.en: The word extends to concrete masses, huge airships, and rigid institutions.
items.cn: 该词扩大指混凝土巨物、巨型飞艇以及僵化的机构。

items.en: Computing then borrows it for software built as one united block.
items.cn: 计算机领域又借用它指作为单一整体构建的软件。

note.en: Monolith is the one-stone noun, close to its Greek relatives on -lith and to other words for huge fixed structures.
note.cn: monolith 是「一整块石头」的名词，与带 -lith 的希腊语同族词以及各种巨大固定构造词相邻。

entries.definition: made from one stone, or rigid and unchanging
entries.definitionCN: 单块石头制成的；僵化不变的

entries.definition: a large stone used to build an ancient monument
entries.definitionCN: 古代纪念建筑所用的大石

entries.definition: a print made from a drawing on stone
entries.definitionCN: 用石版画印出的版画

entries.definition: a tall four-sided stone pillar with a pointed top
entries.definitionCN: 顶部尖细的四棱石柱

entries.definition: one of the huge stones of a prehistoric monument
entries.definitionCN: 史前纪念建筑用的巨石

entries.definition: a large rock worn smooth by weather rather than shaped by people
entries.definitionCN: 自然磨圆的大石块，并非人工雕成

normalIntro.en: Monolith joins one to stone: the first half means single, the second half means stone.
normalIntro.cn: monolith 把「一」和「石头」拼在一起：前半表示单一，后半表示石头。

normal.en: Monos in Greek means one, so a monolith is a one-piece stone.
normal.cn: 希腊语 monos 意为「单一」，所以 monolith 就是一块整石。

normal.en: The same -lith appears in megalith and lithograph.
normal.cn: 同样的 -lith 也出现在 megalith 与 lithograph 里。
