normal.en: Monolithic adds -ic and means made of one stone or rigid.
normal.cn: monolithic 加上 -ic，表示由整块石头制成或僵化不变。

normal.en: A corporate monolith is an organization that will not budge.
normal.cn: a corporate monolith 指一点也推不动的庞大机构。

normal.en: Compare megalith: a megalith is one great stone among many, a monolith is by definition a single stone.
normal.cn: 对比 megalith：megalith 是许多巨石中的一块，monolith 按定义就是一整块。

abstract.en: Picture a plain room with one enormous grey stone and no door in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间空屋里立着一块巨大的灰色石头，石头上没有门。

abstract.en: See an obelisk rising straight out of a block of rose granite.
abstract.cn: 想象一方尖碑从一整块玫瑰色花岗岩中直接立起。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass tower so seamless that it looks like one solid cube.
abstract.cn: 想象一座玻璃高塔毫无接缝，看去像一整块实心方块。

examples.en: The monolith has stood on the hill for five thousand years.
examples.cn: 这块独石在山丘上矗立了五千年。

examples.en: Engineers lifted the giant monolith onto a steel frame.
examples.cn: 工程师把巨大的独石吊装到钢架上。

examples.en: Reformers want to break up the broadcasting monolith.
examples.cn: 改革者希望拆分这个庞大的广播机构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没挪动」——巨石立在原地怎么推也没挪动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 monos（单独的）+ lithos（石头）→ 希腊语 monolithos → 拉丁语借形 monolithus → 十九世纪英语 monolith，核心义「一整块、不可分割的石头」。

sensesIntro.en: Monolith starts as one huge stone, then names stone-built monuments, massive solid objects, rigid institutions, and finally software written as one block.
sensesIntro.cn: monolith 起初指一整个巨大石块，随后指整石建造的纪念物、巨型的实体、僵化的机构，最后指写成一整块的软件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one gigantic unbroken block of stone that cannot be pushed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块、没有接缝、推也推不倒的巨石。

branches.en: The literal stone and the monument built from it share one imagery.
branches.cn: 字面上的石块与用整石建造的纪念物共用同一意象。

branches.en: Any enormous object that looks seamless is described with the stone.
branches.cn: 任何看起来毫无接缝的巨大物体都可以用这块石头来比喻。

branches.en: Institutions borrow the image to suggest rigidity and monopoly.
branches.cn: 机构借用这一意象来表示僵化与垄断。

branches.en: Software in one block repeats the same idea in code.
branches.cn: 一体式软件把同一思路搬进了代码里。

branches.en: Both a stone block and a monolithic program are praised or blamed for being unsplittable.
branches.cn: 整块石头和单体程序都是因为「拆不开」而被称赞或被批评。

intro.en: Monolith is a Greek compound of the combining form mono- and the root -lith, and English builds monolithic from its base.
intro.cn: monolith 是希腊语复合词，由组合形式 mono- 与词根 -lith 组成，英语又在其词基上构成 monolithic。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek rather than Latin; only the borrowed Latin adjective monolithus links the word to Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 各部分属于希腊语而非拉丁语；只有借用的拉丁形容词 monolithus 把该词与拉丁语联系起来。

items.example: The prefix mono- means alone or single in compounds.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mono- 在复合词中意为「单独、单一」。

items.example: The root -lith means stone in geological words.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -lith 在地质词汇中表示石头。

items.example: Monolithos was used of statues from a single block.
items.exampleCN: monolithos 曾用来指用单块石头雕成的雕像。

items.example: The Latin form monolithus describes single-stone work.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁形式 monolithus 描述单块石头做成的东西。

items.meaning: a single stone or a rigid whole
items.example: Monolith entered English in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: monolith 于十九世纪进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -ic gives monolithic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成了 monolithic。

items.meaning: made of one stone or rigidly unified
items.example: Monolithic describes a system that will not bend.
items.exampleCN: monolithic 形容一个不肯变通的体系。

items.example: The suffix -ly gives monolithically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成了 monolithically。

items.example: The system behaves monolithically when stressed.
items.exampleCN: 这个体系在压力下表现为铁板一块。

items.example: Megalith shares the stone root with monolith.
items.exampleCN: megalith 与 monolith 共享「石头」这个词根。

definition_zh: 独白；长篇独白；独角戏；自言自语
definition_en: a long speech made by one person while others listen or stay silent
core_image: 台上只有一个人的灯光，他把整段话全说完，台下无人应答
scene: 夜里排练到很晚，演员站在空台口，把整段台词一个人说完。Late at night the actor stands alone on the empty stage and delivers a long monologue without reply.
sceneCN: 这里 monologue 是「独白」（第 1 个义项：剧中一人独说的长篇台词）；句意：深夜演员独自站在空荡的舞台上，说出一段无人应答的长篇独白。

collocations.phrase: a long monologue about the past
turn a monologue into a dialogue

derivatives.zh: 由 monologue 加 -ist 构成，义为「独白表演者、独白作家」
monologue 加 -u- 与 -ist 的异体拼法，义为「独角独白演员」
由 monologue 加 -ic 构成，义为「独白的；单向独语式的」

senses.title: A long speech by one speaker
senses.definition: a long speech made by one person while others listen silently
senses.definitionCN: 一个人说、别人沉默倾听的长篇讲话
senses.example: Her opening monologue ran for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的开场独白讲了整整十分钟。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean alone plus speech, so the word first names speech in which only one voice is heard.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语两个成分意为「独自」加「说话」，所以这个词首先指只有一种声音的讲话。

senses.title: A speech in drama
senses.definition: a long speech by a character in a play, talking alone or thinking aloud
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧中某个角色独自或在旁人面前长篇自述的台词
senses.example: The dying king keeps the stage for his last monologue.
senses.exampleCN: 将死的国王独自占据舞台，说完最后一段独白。
senses.why: Drama formalized the one-voice speech as a technical term: a character addresses the audience or the air while everyone else falls silent.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧把「只有一个人在说」固定为专门术语：角色对观众或对空发言，其余人都沉默。

senses.title: A talk plus other turns
senses.definition: an entertainment in which one performer gives the whole programme, often with comic stories and voices
senses.definitionCN: 由一人承担全场、常以故事和模仿口吻为主的表演形式
senses.example: His one-man monologue has played for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的单人独角戏已经上演多年。
senses.why: Stage comedy took the word for a whole solo act, so monologue can now name a performance rather than only a passage of speech.
senses.whyCN: 舞台喜剧把这个词用在一整场个人表演上，所以 monologue 现在也可以指一种表演形式，而不只是台词片段。

senses.title: Talking without answers
senses.definition: an instance of speaking at length to someone who cannot or does not reply
senses.definitionCN: 对无法或不愿回应的人长时间讲话的情形
senses.example: My remarks fell into a polite monologue.
senses.exampleCN: 我的问题换来了一段礼貌的独白。
senses.why: Because one voice carries on and the other stays quiet, the word in everyday speech carries a complaint about a talk that is really one-sided.
senses.whyCN: 因为只有一方不断说、另一方默不做声，这个词在日常中常带有抱怨「只有单向发话」的意味。

intro.en: Monologue combines Greek monos, single, with logos, word or speech; the Greek compound monologos is attested, and English monologue is recorded from the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, though monologue became common only in the nineteenth.
intro.cn: monologue 由希腊语 monos（单一）与 logos（言语、话）构成；希腊语复合词 monologos 有文献可证，英语 monologue 于十六至十七世纪已有记录，但到十九世纪才普遍使用。

items.en: Monos means alone, and logos means speech or word.
items.cn: monos 意为「独自」，logos 意为「言语、话」。

items.en: Monologos describes speech that one person makes on their own.
items.cn: monologos 描述由个人单独说出的话。

items.en: Latin writers use monologium for a single voice speaking.
items.cn: 拉丁语作者用 monologium 指单一的声音说话。

items.en: French monologue enters the language of the stage.
items.cn: 法语 monologue 进入舞台语言。

items.en: Monologue appears in English, at first beside the older soliloquy.
items.cn: monologue 进入英语，起初与更早的 soliloquy 并用。

items.en: Modern English extends it to comic acts and everyday one-sided talking.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到喜剧表演与日常的单向讲话。

note.en: Monologue is the one-voice speech noun, close to its -logue relatives and to the drama words for speaking alone.
note.cn: monologue 是「一人独说」的名词，与带 -logue 的同族词以及戏剧中「独自说话」的词汇相邻。

entries.definition: a conversation between two or more people
entries.definitionCN: 两人或更多人的对话

entries.definition: an opening section before the main work
entries.definitionCN: 正文之前的开场部分

entries.definition: a person who speaks alone or performs a monologue
entries.definitionCN: 独白者；独角戏演员

entries.definition: a speech in a play where a character speaks their thoughts aloud
entries.definitionCN: 剧中角色吐露心声的独白

entries.definition: a long talk given to teach or scold
entries.definitionCN: 用于讲授或训诫的长篇讲话

entries.definition: a short remark in a play that other characters do not hear
entries.definitionCN: 剧中旁人听不到的简短插话

normalIntro.en: Monologue joins alone to speech: one speaker, one voice, and no answer coming back.
normalIntro.cn: monologue 把「独自」和「言语」拼在一起：一个说话人、一种声音，没有回应回来。

normal.en: The first part means alone, so a monologue is talk by one voice.
normal.cn: 前半表示「独自」，所以 monologue 是一种声音的讲话。

normal.en: Dialogue and prologue share the -logue root for speech.
normal.cn: dialogue 与 prologue 共享表示「言语」的 -logue 词根。

normal.en: Monologist names the performer, not the speech.
normal.cn: monologist 指的是表演者，而不是那段话。

normal.en: To launch into a monologue is to start talking and not stop.
normal.cn: launch into a monologue 就是开口就停不下来。

normal.en: Compare soliloquy: a soliloquy is spoken alone in thought, a monologue is long speech by one voice in front of others.
normal.cn: 对比 soliloquy：前者是独自吐露心声，后者是在他人面前由一人说出的大段讲话。

abstract.en: Picture one spotlight on a stage and every other chair empty.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台上只有一束追光，其余椅子都空着。

abstract.en: Hear a caller talking on and on while the phone stays silent at the other end.
abstract.cn: 想象电话这头的人滔滔不绝，另一端始终没有声音。

abstract.en: See a poem in which one invented speaker addresses the reader alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一首诗里只有一个虚构的说话人，独自对读者发话。

examples.en: The comedian opened with a monologue about trains.
examples.cn: 喜剧演员以一段关于火车的独白开场。

examples.en: He delivered the monologue so quietly that the back row missed it.
examples.cn: 他的独白说得太轻，后排几乎没听见。

examples.en: Her mother answered every question with a long monologue.
examples.cn: 她母亲对每个问题都以一长串自言自语作答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「默闹唠」——一个人闷着头闹着、唠唠叨叨说不停，全是独白；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 monos（单独的）+ logos（言语、话）→ 希腊语 monologos → 晚期拉丁语 monologium → 法语 monologue → 英语 monologue，核心义「一个人独自说的长篇话」。

sensesIntro.en: Monologue first means a long speech by one speaker, then a dramatic speech, a solo act, and finally everyday talk that gets no reply.
sensesIntro.cn: monologue 先指一人独说的长篇讲话，再指戏剧独白、独角表演，最后指日常生活中得不到回应的单向絮语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lighted speaker on a stage while the others stay silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台上一人被灯照着说话，其余人都沉默。

branches.en: The basic meaning is a long talk by one speaker.
branches.cn: 基本义就是一人独说的长篇讲话。

branches.en: Drama turns the basic meaning into a fixed stage term.
branches.cn: 戏剧把基本义固定成舞台术语。

branches.en: A whole act by one performer grows out of the one-voice idea.
branches.cn: 一人的整场表演从「单一声音」这一想法生长出来。

branches.en: In daily talk the word hints that the other person was never heard.
branches.cn: 在日常言谈中，这个词暗示另一个人始终没有被听见。

branches.en: Speech, stage, and real life all repeat the picture of one voice and a silent audience.
branches.cn: 言语、舞台与现实生活都在重复「一种声音对沉默听众」的画面。

intro.en: Monologue is a Greek compound of mono- and the -logue root for speech, and English builds monologist and monologic on its base.
intro.cn: monologue 是希腊语复合词，由 mono- 与表示「言语」的 -logue 词根构成，英语又在其词基上构成 monologist 与 monologic。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, though Late Latin monologium carried the compound into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 各部分属于希腊语，不过晚期拉丁语 monologium 把这个复合词带进了欧洲各语言。

items.example: The prefix mono- appears in words for one thing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mono- 出现在表示「单一」的词中。

items.example: The root -logue means speech in dialogue and prologue.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -logue 在 dialogue 与 prologue 中表示言语。

items.example: Logos supplies the speech part of the word.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供了该词中「言语」这一部分。

items.example: Monologos describes speech with no partner.
items.exampleCN: monologos 描述没有对话方的讲话。

items.example: Monologium is the Latin form of the compound.
items.exampleCN: monologium 是该复合词的拉丁形式。

items.meaning: a long speech by one speaker
items.example: Monologue became common on the English stage.
items.exampleCN: monologue 在英语舞台上变得常用。

items.example: The suffix -ist gives monologist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成了 monologist。

items.example: A monologist addresses the room alone.
items.exampleCN: 独白者独自面对着全场说话。

items.example: The suffix -ic gives monologic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 构成了 monologic。

items.meaning: in the form of a monologue
items.example: Monologic writing lets one voice carry the text.
items.exampleCN: 独白式写作让一种声音撑起全文。

items.example: The prefix dia- turns dialogue into talk between speakers.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dia- 让 dialogue 成为说话者之间的交谈。

definition_zh: 单调的；枯燥乏味的；一成不变的；音调单一的
definition_en: boring because it never changes and always stays the same
core_image: 一条没有起伏的直线：声音或日子一直平着走，不起波澜
scene: 工厂流水线上，工人每天重复同一个动作，听同一种机器声。On the assembly line, the same action and the same hum fill every hour of the day, so the work feels monotonous.
sceneCN: 这里 monotonous 是「单调乏味」（第 1 个义项：因毫无变化而令人厌烦）；句意：流水线上同样的动作与同样的嗡嗡声填满每个时段，工作因此显得单调乏味。

pos.zh: 单调的；枯燥乏味的；音调单一的

derivatives.zh: 由单调词根加 -y 构成的名词，义为「单调；乏味」
monotonous 去掉 -ous 加 -ously 构成的副词，义为「单调地；千篇一律地」
由 mono- 与 tone 构成的词，义为「单调的声音；平板的语调」

senses.title: Boring because nothing changes
senses.definition: dull and tiring because it never varies and is always the same
senses.definitionCN: 因为毫无变化、总是老样子而令人厌倦
senses.example: The long drive across the plain became monotonous.
senses.exampleCN: 穿越平原的长途车程变得单调乏味。
senses.why: The Greek parts mean one tone, and a sound or task that keeps a single pitch soon bores the ear and the mind.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语两个成分意为「一个音调」，一直停在同一个调子上的声音或工作，很快就会让耳朵和心思发腻。

senses.title: Unvarying in pitch
senses.definition: spoken or played on a single level, without rises, falls, or emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 说话或演奏始终在同一音高上，没有高低起伏和重音
senses.example: He read the notice in a flat, monotonous voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他用平淡单调的声音念了通知。
senses.why: This is the loosest sense, still close to the original musical one, and it is why a dull speaker sounds like a single held note.
senses.whyCN: 这是最贴近原义的用法，仍保留音乐含义，所以乏味的演讲者听上去像一个拖着的单音。

senses.title: Repeating without relief
senses.definition: repeating the same pattern again and again so that nothing stands out
senses.definitionCN: 同一个模式反复出现，什么也不突出
senses.example: The town has a monotonous row of identical houses.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上有一排千篇一律、一模一样的小房子。
senses.why: The one-tone image extends from sound to patterns: when every item looks or happens just like the last, the eye and the day lose their rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 「单音」的意象从声音扩展到模式：当每一件事都和上一件一模一样，眼睛和日子就失去了节拍。

senses.title: In bookish use: in one tone
senses.definition: produced or written in one continuous tone, as in old rhetoric and music writing
senses.definitionCN: 以同一个连续的音调说出或写就，见于古老的修辞与音乐论著
senses.example: The old manual calls a single-pitch chant monotonous.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧手册把单音高的吟唱称作单声调的。
senses.why: Rhetoric and music theory first used the word technically for recitation on one pitch, before everyday speech took it over.
senses.whyCN: 修辞学与乐理最初把它作为术语，指在同一个音高上诵读，后来才被日常语言接收。

intro.en: Monotonous comes from Late Latin monotonus, from Greek monos, single, plus tonos, a pitch or tone; the word first belonged to music and rhetoric and only later meant boring.
intro.cn: monotonous 来自晚期拉丁语 monotonus，源于希腊语 monos（单一）加 tonos（音高、调）；该词最初属于音乐与修辞学，后来才表示「乏味」。

items.en: Monos means one, and tonos means a pitch or stretched string.
items.cn: monos 意为「一」，tonos 意为音高或绷紧的弦。

items.en: Monotonos means sounding on a single pitch.
items.cn: monotonos 意为在单一音高上发声。

items.en: Latin writers borrow the adjective as monotonus.
items.cn: 拉丁语作者借入该形容词为 monotonus。

items.en: English uses monotonous for recitation and chant on one note.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语把 monotonous 用于单音高的诵读与吟唱。

items.en: Rhetoric books extend it to flat, undramatic prose.
items.cn: 十九世纪的修辞书把它扩展到平淡无起伏的散文。

items.en: Modern English carries the meaning over to dull work, food, and routines.
items.cn: 现代英语把「乏味」之意延伸到枯燥的工作、饮食与日常。

note.en: Monotonous is the one-tone adjective, close to its -tone relatives and to other words for dull sameness.
note.cn: monotonous 是表示「单一个调」的形容词，与带 tone 的同族词以及各种表示乏味的词相邻。

entries.definition: the quality of being dull and unchanging
entries.definitionCN: 单调；乏味

entries.definition: a sound or voice that stays on one level
entries.definitionCN: 平板的语调或单一的音

entries.definition: in a dull, unvarying way
entries.definitionCN: 单调地；千篇一律地

entries.definition: long and tiring because it is dull
entries.definitionCN: 冗长而乏味的

entries.definition: not interesting or stimulating
entries.definitionCN: 无聊的；没有兴味的

entries.definition: always staying the same
entries.definitionCN: 始终不变的

normalIntro.en: Monotonous joins one to tone: a single unbroken pitch that never rises or falls.
normalIntro.cn: monotonous 把「一」和「调子」拼在一起：一个从不升起也不落下的声音。

normal.en: The first part means one, so monotonous is one tone and no variation.
normal.cn: 前半表示「一」，所以 monotonous 就是一个调子、毫无变化。

normal.en: The tone part links it to monotone and to the music term tonic.
normal.cn: 其中的 tone 部分把它与 monotone 以及音乐术语 tonic 连在一起。

normal.en: The noun monotony drops the -ous and names the quality.
normal.cn: 名词 monotony 去掉 -ous，指这种性质本身。

normal.en: A monotonous voice sounds like one long held note.
normal.cn: a monotonous voice 听上去像拖着一个长长的单音。

normal.en: Compare tedious: tedious tires you with length, monotonous tires you with sameness.
normal.cn: 对比 tedious：tedious 因冗长而累人，monotonous 因千篇一律而累人。

abstract.en: Picture a heart monitor that draws a dead flat line.
abstract.cn: 想象一台监护仪上画出一条完全平直的线。

abstract.en: Hear one beep repeated with no pause and no rise in pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个哔声不停重复，不停顿也不升高。

abstract.en: See the same grey wall passing for hour after hour on a bus.
abstract.cn: 想象坐大巴时一堵同样的灰墙一小时又一小时地掠过。

examples.en: The lecture was so monotonous that half the class fell asleep.
examples.cn: 讲座单调得让半班学生都睡着了。

examples.en: He answered in a monotonous voice that never changed.
examples.cn: 他用始终不变的单调嗓音回答。

examples.en: Her days at the new job soon felt monotonous.
examples.cn: 她在新岗位上没过多久就觉得日子枯燥乏味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫挪态」——一成不变、连动都不想挪，就这么单调着；这只是拆词谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 monos（单一）+ tonos（音高、调）→ 希腊语 monotonos（单音调的）→ 晚期拉丁语 monotonus → 英语 monotonous，核心义「只有一个调、毫无起伏」。

sensesIntro.en: Monotonous starts with speech and music on a single pitch, then extends to patterns that never change and finally to anything boringly the same.
sensesIntro.cn: monotonous 起初指说话与音乐停在单一音高上，随后扩展到反复不变的样式，最后泛指任何无聊的千篇一律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single note held on one pitch, with no rise or fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个音高上拖住不放的单音，既不上扬也不下落。

branches.en: The general sense is dullness born from sameness.
branches.cn: 一般义就是由千篇一律而来的乏味。

branches.en: The technical senses stay close to the musical single tone.
branches.cn: 技术与书面义项仍紧贴音乐上的单音。

branches.en: Repeated patterns make the eye lose rhythm just as one tone tires the ear.
branches.cn: 重复的样式让眼睛失去节拍，正如单音让耳朵发腻。

branches.en: Dull work and dull scenery share the same flat, unbroken line.
branches.cn: 枯燥的工作与单调的风景共用同一条平坦不断的直线。

branches.en: A flat voice and a flat diet both lack the rise and spark that variety gives.
branches.cn: 平板的嗓音和乏味的饮食都缺少变化带来的起伏与亮色。

intro.en: Monotonous is built from mono- plus the tone root, with the suffix -ous adding the idea of having that quality.
intro.cn: monotonous 由 mono- 加 tone 词根构成，后缀 -ous 表示「具有这种性质」。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, and Late Latin monotonus passed the adjective on to English.
latinIntro.cn: 各部分属于希腊语，晚期拉丁语 monotonus 把这个形容词传给了英语。

items.example: The prefix mono- means one in countless compounds.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mono- 在大量复合词中表示「一」。

items.example: Tonos gives the tone root in English.
items.exampleCN: tonos 提供了英语中的 tone 词根。

items.example: The suffix -ous marks an adjective of quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 标示表示性质的形容词。

items.example: Monotonos described a single-pitch recitation.
items.exampleCN: monotonos 描述单音高的诵读。

items.example: Monotonus carried the word into Latin.
items.exampleCN: monotonus 把这个词带入拉丁语。

definition_zh: 怪物；怪兽；庞然大物；小恶魔；令人恐惧的东西
definition_en: a large frightening imaginary creature, a very large or ugly thing, or a cruel person
core_image: 阴影里探出一张巨大的怪脸，张着嘴，比周围的一切都大
scene: 半夜，阁楼的阴影里传来一声低吼，孩子缩进被子里，坚信床下蹲着一头怪物。In the night, a growl came from the attic shadows, and the child hid under the quilt, sure that a monster was crouching under the bed.
sceneCN: 这里 monster 是「怪物」（第 1 个义项：想象中巨大可怕的生物）；句意：半夜阁楼传来低吼，孩子躲进被子里，以为床下蹲着一头怪物。

pos.zh: 怪物；怪兽；庞然大物；小恶魔；令人恐惧的人或物
巨大的；特大号的（多用于 monster truck、monster wave 等复合词）

collocations.zh: 小捣蛋（对淘气小孩的戏称）
嫉妒（莎士比亚用语，指嫉妒心）

加 -osity 构成的名词，义为「怪物；丑恶而庞大的东西」
