senses.title: A frightening imaginary creature
senses.definition: a large, ugly or frightening creature from stories, films or myths
senses.definitionCN: 传说、故事或影视中巨大、丑陋、可怕的生物
senses.example: The movie shows a monster living in the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影讲的是湖里住着一头怪物。
senses.why: The Latin source monstrum named a divine omen warning of trouble, and a being that brings bad news easily becomes a fright.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monstrum 原指预示灾祸的神兆，而带来凶讯的存在很容易被想象成吓人的东西，于是有了「怪物」这一义。

senses.title: A very large thing
senses.definition: a thing or vehicle that is much larger than others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 比同类大得多的东西或车辆
senses.example: A monster truck rolled over the parked cars.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆巨型卡车碾过了停放的车。
senses.why: Because monsters are imagined as enormous, the word shifted from the creature itself to anything oversized.
senses.whyCN: 怪物在想象中总是巨大无比，所以词义从生物本体延伸到任何超大号的东西。

senses.title: A cruel person
senses.definition: a person who behaves in a cruel or evil way
senses.definitionCN: 行为残忍或邪恶的人
senses.example: The judge called the killer a monster.
senses.exampleCN: 法官称这个杀人犯为恶魔。
senses.why: Once a monster is a figure of fear, it is a short step to calling a heartless person by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 怪物一旦成了恐惧的象征，把没有心肝的人也叫作怪物，只有一步之遥。

senses.title: A naughty child
senses.definition: a child who behaves badly but is usually spoken of with affection
senses.definitionCN: 调皮捣蛋的孩子，通常带亲昵语气
senses.example: The little monster poured paint on the carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小捣蛋把颜料倒在了地毯上。
senses.why: Adults soften the fearsome word into a joke, so a lively child becomes a little monster.
senses.whyCN: 大人把这个可怕的词当成玩笑用，于是活泼淘气的孩子就成了「小捣蛋」。

senses.title: A very ugly object
senses.definition: an object so ugly or badly built that it shocks people
senses.definitionCN: 极其丑陋或粗制滥造、令人惊愕的物体
senses.example: The new shopping centre is a concrete monster.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新购物中心就是一座混凝土怪物。
senses.why: The shock value of a monster transfers to ugly buildings and machines that dominate the skyline.
senses.whyCN: 怪物带来的惊骇感转移到霸占天际线的丑陋建筑和机器上，于是有了「巨型丑物」义。

senses.title: A powerful force
senses.definition: something that seems impossible to control because of its size or power
senses.definitionCN: 因规模或力量巨大而似乎无法控制的事物
senses.example: Inflation had become a monster that wrecked household budgets.
senses.exampleCN: 通货膨胀已变成一头摧毁家庭预算的怪物。
senses.why: What cannot be tamed and keeps growing gets the name of a monster in journalism and politics.
senses.whyCN: 新闻和政治评论常把无法驯服、不断膨胀的东西称作怪物，于是这个义项从怪物意象自然延伸而来。

senses.title: An enormous serving
senses.definition: an extremely large version of a product, especially food or a drink
senses.definitionCN: 某产品（尤指食物或饮料）的超大版本
senses.example: We shared a monster pizza at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上我们分享了一张超大号披萨。
senses.why: Modern marketing borrows the word as an adjective meaning huge, so a serving can itself be a monster.
senses.whyCN: 现代营销借这个词作形容词表示「巨大」，于是份量本身也可以叫 monster。

senses.title: A shocking deed
senses.definition: a crime or event so cruel or strange that it shocks people
senses.definitionCN: 极其残忍或离奇、令人震惊的罪行或事件
senses.example: The novel describes a monster of greed and cruelty.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说描写了一桩集贪婪与残忍于一体的骇人恶行。
senses.why: The old omen sense survives as a warning of horror, so a shocking crime can be called a monster.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「凶兆」含义以骇人的方式留存下来，因此令人震惊的罪行也可以被称作怪物般的事。

intro.en: Monster comes from Latin monstrum, a divine portent or omen, from monere, to warn; Old French monstre carries it into English.
intro.cn: monster 来自拉丁语 monstrum（神兆、预兆），源于 monere（警告）；经古法语 monstre 进入英语。

items.en: Monere means to warn or remind, the root later found in monitor and admonish.
items.cn: monere 意为警告、提醒，这一词根后来也见于 monitor 与 admonish。

items.en: Monstrum names a sign sent by the gods to show divine anger or a coming disaster.
items.cn: monstrum 指神明显怒或预示灾难而发出的征兆。

items.en: Monstra also comes to mean unnatural or deformed creatures, seen as such signs.
items.cn: monstra 后来又指畸形的、不合常理的生物，因为这些生物被视为预兆。

items.en: Monstre reaches French, naming a monster, a marvel or a deformed animal as well as bad luck.
items.cn: monstre 进入法语，既指怪物、奇观、畸形动物，也指厄运。

items.en: Monster appears in Middle English first as an animal or being that breaks the order of nature.
items.cn: monster 在中古英语中先用来指违背自然秩序的动物或存在。

items.en: The modern word widens to oversized things, cruel people, and commercial superlatives.
items.cn: 现代英语进一步扩展，指超大物体、残忍之人和商业上的「超大型」说法。

note.en: Monster links to monstrous and monstrosity on one side, and to beast, creature and ogre as near meanings on the other.
note.cn: monster 一边连着 monstrous 与 monstrosity 等派生词，一边与 beast、creature、ogre 等近义词相邻。

entries.definition: very large, ugly or shocking
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的；骇人的；丑陋的（由 monster 加 -ous 构成）

entries.definition: something huge and ugly
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而丑陋的东西；怪物

entries.definition: to show clearly how something works
entries.definitionCN: 演示；证明（只是拼写中段相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a wild or frightening animal
entries.definitionCN: 野兽；凶猛的动物

entries.definition: any living thing, often an imaginary one
entries.definitionCN: 生物；（常指想象的）造物

entries.definition: a cruel giant in fairy tales
entries.definitionCN: 童话中的食人巨怪

normalIntro.en: Monster grew out of the Latin warning word monere, so the creature is literally a sign shown to scare.
normalIntro.cn: monster 源自拉丁语警告词 monere，所以这种生物本身就是用吓人来示警的征兆。

normal.en: Monere, to warn, is the same root as monitor and admonish.
normal.cn: 表「警告」的 monere 与 monitor、admonish 同源，可一起记。

normal.en: Monstrous is the adjective and monstrosity the noun of the same family.
normal.cn: monstrous 是同族的形容词，monstrosity 是同族的名词。

normal.en: Monster movie and sea monster keep the old image of an unnatural beast.
normal.cn: 「怪兽电影」与「海怪」保留了「违背自然的野兽」这一旧意象。

normal.en: The green-eyed monster, a phrase from Shakespeare, means jealousy.
normal.cn: green-eyed monster 出自莎士比亚，指嫉妒心。

normal.en: Do not mix monster with demonstrate and remonstrate, which only share the middle letters.
normal.cn: 不要把 monster 与 demonstrate、remonstrate 混记，它们只是中段字母相似。

abstract.en: See a warning signpost in a dark wood that suddenly grows eyes and teeth.
abstract.cn: 想象幽暗林间一块警告路牌突然长出了眼睛和牙齿。

abstract.en: Picture a toy truck swelling until it fills the whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆玩具卡车不断膨胀，最后占满整条街。

abstract.en: Imagine a kind face turning cold and cruel like a mask slipping off.
abstract.cn: 想象一张和善的脸变得冷酷残忍，像面具滑落。

examples.en: Legend says a monster guards the old bridge at night.
examples.cn: 传说夜里有一头怪物守着那座老桥。

examples.en: Critics called the tower a concrete monster that blocked the view.
examples.cn: 评论家称这座塔为混凝土怪物，挡住了风景。

examples.en: The villagers had turned the little monsters into a bedtime story.
examples.cn: 村民们把这些小怪物变成了哄睡的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「门斯特」——门后面藏着斯特拉样的怪兽；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 monere（警告、提醒）→ monstrum（神兆；异象；怪胎）→ 古法语 monstre → 英语 monster，核心义「以骇人形象现形的凶兆」。

sensesIntro.en: Monster starts as a warning creature, widens to anything huge or ugly, extends to cruel people and naughty children, and ends as a figurative force or a marketing superlative.
sensesIntro.cn: monster 先指示警的异类生物，再扩大到任何巨大或丑陋的东西，又延伸到残忍之人和淘气孩子，最后成为比喻性的力量或营销里的「超大」说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a huge shadowed face looming in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中浮现一张巨大的怪脸。

branches.en: The story creature is the original sense.
branches.cn: 故事里的怪兽是本源义。

branches.en: Size and ugliness turn the creature name into a label for things.
branches.cn: 体积与丑陋让这个生物名称变成物品的标签。

branches.en: Human cruelty and childish mischief both borrow the name.
branches.cn: 人的残忍与小孩的顽皮都借用了这个名字。

branches.en: Untamed forces and shocking deeds inherit the omen of horror.
branches.cn: 失控的力量与骇人的行径继承了凶兆带来的恐惧。

branches.en: Marketing uses the monster mainly as a word for huge.
branches.cn: 商业营销主要把 monster 当作「巨大」的代称。

intro.en: Monster is a Latin-derived word built on the root mon, to warn, with English family words monstrous, monstrosity and monstrously.
intro.cn: monster 是拉丁语来源的词，建立在「警告」词根 mon 之上，英语词族有 monstrous、monstrosity 与 monstrously。

latinIntro.en: Latin monere means to warn, monstrum means an omen, and monstra also names deformed creatures.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 monere 意为警告，monstrum 意为预兆，monstra 也指畸形生物。

items.example: The root mon- links monster to monitor and admonish.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mon- 把 monster 与 monitor、admonish 连在一起。

items.example: Monere gives the idea of a warning.
items.exampleCN: monere 提供「警告」的含义。

items.example: Monstrum first names a divine sign.
items.exampleCN: monstrum 最初指神示。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous turns monster into monstrous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把 monster 变成 monstrous。

items.example: Monstrous describes something too big to accept.
items.exampleCN: monstrous 描述大到难以接受的东西。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity helps form monstrosity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 帮助构成 monstrosity。

items.example: Monstrosity names an ugly oversized thing.
items.exampleCN: monstrosity 指丑陋硕大的东西。

items.meaning: in a certain manner, forming adverbs
items.example: The suffix -ly forms monstrously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 monstrously。

items.example: Monstrously means to an extreme degree.
items.exampleCN: monstrously 表示到了极端程度。

definition_zh: 蒙太奇；剪辑组接；拼贴组合；组合照片
definition_en: a technique of assembling separate images, shots or fragments into one continuous whole, or the work so made
core_image: 许多张照片被剪刀剪开，再拼贴成一幅完整的画面
scene: 导演把雨夜的街道、奔跑的狗和亮起的窗户快速剪在一起，几十秒的镜头组接就交代完了一整年的生活。The director cut the rainy street, the running dog and the lit windows in quick succession, and a thirty-second montage told a whole year of life.
sceneCN: 这里 montage 是「蒙太奇」（第 2 个义项：影视中把若干镜头组接成连续段落）；句意：导演把雨夜街道、奔跑的狗与亮起的窗户快速剪在一起，几十秒的蒙太奇讲完了一整年的生活。

pos.zh: 蒙太奇；剪辑组接；拼贴组合；组合照片
把……剪辑组接起来；拼贴制作

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -ist 构成，义为「擅长蒙太奇手法的人」
photo 与 montage 复合而成，义为「照片剪辑拼贴」
拼贴画；源自法语，与 montage 同属「拼接」义场，但拼的是平面材料

senses.title: A pasted-together picture
senses.definition: a picture made by pasting separate images or parts onto one surface
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的图像或部件粘贴在同一平面上而成的图画
senses.example: The gallery wall held a montage of old postcards.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊的墙上挂着一幅由旧明信片拼成的拼贴画。
senses.why: French monter means to mount or put up, and a montage first names pictures mounted up together on one board.
senses.whyCN: 法语 monter 意为「装上去、架起」，所以 montage 最初指把图片装上同一块板子拼成一张图，这就是拼贴义。

senses.title: A film sequence of joined shots
senses.definition: a sequence in a film or video made by editing separate shots together to compress time or suggest meaning
senses.definitionCN: 影视中把分开的镜头剪辑组接、用来压缩时间或暗示含义的段落
senses.example: The training montage showed months of practice in two minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 训练蒙太奇用两分钟呈现了几个月的练习。
senses.why: Filmmakers borrowed the term for shots mounted side by side, and the idea that meaning arises between shots became the core of the cinema sense.
senses.whyCN: 电影人借这个词指并排组接的镜头，而「含义在镜头之间产生」成了这一影视义项的核心。

senses.title: Any mixture of fragments
senses.definition: a mixture of different pieces of writing, music, memories or images assembled into a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的文字、音乐、记忆或图像片段组装成一个整体
senses.example: The essay reads like a montage of voices and diary entries.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章读起来像由多种声音和日记片段拼接而成。
senses.why: If images can be mounted together, so can words, sounds and memories, which widens the word beyond pictures.
senses.whyCN: 既然图像可以拼装，文字、声音和记忆也可以拼装，于是词义超出了图像范围，得到「混合片段」义。

senses.title: The editing method itself
senses.definition: the technique or principle of constructing a rapid, associative sequence out of separate elements
senses.definitionCN: 用分散元素快速、联想式地构造连贯整体的技法或原则
senses.example: Eisenstein argued that montage could create ideas that no single shot could.
senses.exampleCN: 爱森斯坦认为蒙太奇能创造任何单个镜头都无法产生的思想。
senses.why: From the product the word moves to the method, so critics can discuss montage as a craft and a theory.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「成品」转向「做法」，所以评论家可以把蒙太奇当作一种手艺与理论来讨论。

senses.title: An assembly of varied items
senses.definition: a deliberately assembled group of varied things presented as a set
senses.definitionCN: 有意组装起来、作为一个整体呈现的各类事物
senses.example: The menu was a montage of dishes from three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这份菜单汇集了来自三个大洲的菜肴。
senses.why: The French verb also means to assemble pieces, so any carefully arranged set of items can be called a montage.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语动词也指「组装部件」，因此任何经过精心排列的成套物件都可以叫作 montage。

senses.title: A rapid succession of images
senses.definition: a fast, overlapping flow of images that a person sees or remembers
senses.definitionCN: 人看到或回忆起的一连串快速交叠的画面
senses.example: His memory was a montage of airport queues and hotel rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 他的记忆是一连串机场排队与酒店房间的画面。
senses.why: The editing sense loosens into a way of describing experience itself as a fast-cut film.
senses.whyCN: 剪辑义进一步泛化，把亲身经历也描述成像快切影片一样，于是有了「接踵画面」义。

intro.en: Montage comes from French monter, to go up or to mount, and first meant the mounting of pictures; cinema criticism gave it its modern sense.
intro.cn: montage 来自法语 monter（上升；装上），最初指装裱、拼装图片；电影评论赋予了它现代含义。

items.en: Mons, montis means a mountain, and montare means to go up or climb.
items.cn: mons、montis 意为山，montare 意为登上、爬升。

items.en: Monter develops in French to mean to mount, to set up or to fit parts together.
items.cn: 法语 monter 发展出「装上、架设、把部件装配起来」的含义。

items.en: Montage in art and architecture names the act of mounting or assembling pieces into a whole.
items.cn: 在艺术与建筑领域，montage 指把部件装上、组合成一个整体。

items.en: Film theorists in France and Soviet cinema use montage for the editing of shots into sequences.
items.cn: 法国电影理论家与苏联电影学派用 montage 指把镜头剪接成段落。

items.en: English takes montage first as the selection and arrangement of film, then widens it to any assembled set.
items.cn: 英语先以 montage 指影片的拣选与组接，随后扩展到任何拼装的组合。

items.en: Today montage also covers photomontage, music and everyday memories, and is even used as a verb.
items.cn: 如今 montage 也涵盖照片拼贴、音乐拼接与日常记忆，甚至可以用作动词。

note.en: Montage looks like its French relatives collage, photomontage and monter, and is close in meaning to sequence and editing.
note.cn: montage 在拼写上与法语同源词 collage、photomontage、monter 相邻，在意义上与 sequence、editing 等说法接近。

entries.definition: a picture made by sticking materials onto a surface
entries.definitionCN: 把材料黏贴到平面上做成的拼贴画（同为法语借词，结尾音 -age 相同）

entries.definition: a picture built from combined photographs
entries.definitionCN: 把照片组合拼接成的画面

entries.definition: French verb meaning to mount or assemble
entries.definitionCN: 法语动词，意为装上、装配（montage 的直接词源）

entries.definition: to fix something in place or set it up
entries.definitionCN: 安装；装上（与 montage 同源自拉丁语 montare）

entries.definition: a set of related shots or events in order
entries.definitionCN: 按顺序排列的一组相关镜头或事件

entries.definition: the work of cutting and arranging film or sound
entries.definitionCN: 剪辑工作；影片或声音的剪切与编排

entries.definition: a collection of pieces gathered into one work
entries.definitionCN: 汇编；把片段汇集成一部作品

normalIntro.en: Montage is a French borrowing from monter, to mount, so the whole word is really about mounting pieces side by side until they read as one.
normalIntro.cn: montage 是借自法语 monter（装上）的词，整个词的核心就是「把碎片并排装上，直到读成一个整体」。

normal.en: The -age ending marks a French noun of action, and American speakers stress the second syllable.
normal.cn: 词尾 -age 是法语动作名词的标志，美式发音重音在第二个音节。

normal.en: Monter, to mount, also gives the English verb mount.
normal.cn: 表示装上的法语 monter 也演变成英语动词 mount。

normal.en: Photomontage simply puts photo in front of montage.
normal.cn: photomontage 就是在 montage 前面加上 photo。

normal.en: A montage of followed by a plural noun is a common and useful pattern.
normal.cn: 「a montage of ＋复数名词」是常见且好用的句式。

normal.en: Do not confuse montage with collage and message, which look close but mean different things.
normal.cn: 别把 montage 与 collage、message 混掉，它们外形相近但意思不同。

abstract.en: Picture a photographer pasting postcards onto a cork board until the edges blur.
abstract.cn: 想象一位摄影师把明信片贴满软木板，直到边界模糊。

abstract.en: Picture a film reel cut into strips and shuffled like a deck of cards.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷胶片被剪成条，像纸牌一样被重新洗牌。

abstract.en: Think of a photo album whose pages overlap, each new page partly hiding the old.
abstract.cn: 想象一本相册，页页相叠，新页遮住旧页的一部分。

examples.en: The opening montage takes the hero from boyhood to old age without a word.
examples.cn: 开场蒙太奇一言不发地把主人公从少年带到老年。

examples.en: She framed a montage of family holidays above the fireplace.
examples.cn: 她把一组家庭度假照片拼贴起来，挂在壁炉上方。

examples.en: The exhibition presents a montage of fragments from five decades of music.
examples.cn: 展览把五十年音乐史中的片段拼贴在一起呈现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「蒙太奇」——把一段段画面「蒙」在一起，奇怪的拼接就成大片；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mons（山）→ montare（登上）→ 法语 monter（装上、装配）→ montage（装裱；拼贴）→ 电影剪辑「蒙太奇」，核心义「把碎片装上同一个面」。

sensesIntro.en: Montage begins as mounted pictures, grows into a film technique of joined shots, then loosens into a mixture of fragments, a craft, an assembled set and finally a rapid flow of remembered images.
sensesIntro.cn: montage 起初指装裱拼贴的图像，后来发展为组接镜头的电影技法，再泛化为碎片混合、手法、拼装组合，最后也指记忆里快速闪过的画面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many cut photographs pasted into one picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多剪开的照片拼成一张画。

branches.en: The pasted picture is the earliest physical sense.
branches.cn: 拼贴图画是最早的实体义。

branches.en: Joined shots and the editing principle are the cinematic pair.
branches.cn: 镜头组接与剪辑原则是影视中的一对义项。

branches.en: Any mixture or assembled set extends the pasting idea to other materials.
branches.cn: 任何混合片段或拼装组合都把「拼贴」扩展到其他材料。

branches.en: Remembered images flow like a fast-cut sequence.
branches.cn: 回忆中的画面像快剪段落一样流动。

branches.en: Both the earliest picture and the film sequence rest on separate parts forming one whole.
branches.cn: 最早的拼贴画与电影蒙太奇都建立在「碎片合成整体」之上。

intro.en: Montage is a French loan built on monter, to mount, with English family words montage-like compounds such as photomontage and the verb montage.
intro.cn: montage 是法语借词，建立在 monter（装上）之上，英语词族有 photomontage 之类复合词以及动词用法。

latinIntro.en: Latin mons means mountain and montare means to go up, the base that French monter extends to putting parts in place.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mons 意为山，montare 意为登上，这个基础被法语 monter 延伸到「把部件放到位」。

items.example: The root mont- also appears in mountain and montane.
items.exampleCN: 词根 mont- 也见于 mountain 与 montane。

items.example: Mons is the Latin word for a mountain.
items.exampleCN: mons 是拉丁语中的「山」。

items.example: Montare supplies the idea of mounting.
items.exampleCN: montare 提供「装上、登上」的含义。

items.example: French monter is the direct source of montage.
items.exampleCN: 法语 monter 是 montage 的直接来源。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作或动作结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -age turns a verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -age 把动词变成动作名词。

items.example: Montage carries the noun sense into English.
items.exampleCN: montage 把名词含义带入英语。

items.example: The prefix photo- forms photomontage.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 photo- 构成 photomontage。

items.example: Photomontage joins photos into one design.
items.exampleCN: photomontage 把照片拼成一个设计。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms montagist.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ist 构成 montagist。

items.example: Montagist is a rare but recorded noun.
items.exampleCN: montagist 是少见但有记录的集合名词。

definition_zh: 每月的；按月计算的；月刊；每月一次
definition_en: happening, paid or published once every month, or a publication that appears once a month
core_image: 日历翻过一页，月亮绕地球走完一圈，又回到同一个位置
scene: 月底一到，手机就会推送账单；她把每个月的房租、交通和网费汇总到一张表格里。At the end of every month her phone sends a bill reminder, so she adds the rent, transport and internet costs into one monthly table.
sceneCN: 这里 monthly 是「每月的」（第 1 个义项：每月发生或按月的）；句意：每到月底手机推送账单，她把房租、交通和网费记进一张月度表格。

pos.zh: 每月的；按月的；每月一次的

derivatives.zh: 去掉词尾 -ly 后得到的基础名词，义为「月；月份」
mid 与 month 复合而成，义为「月中」
month 与 long 复合而成，义为「持续一个月的」
前缀 bi-（两；每两）加 monthly，义为「每两月的；每月两次的」，含义需看语境
fortnight 加 -ly 构成，义为「每两周的」，与 monthly 同属时间频率形容词

senses.title: Happening once a month
senses.definition: happening, done or calculated once every month
senses.definitionCN: 每月发生、进行或计算一次的
senses.example: The monthly rent falls due on the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 房租每月一号到期。
senses.why: Month comes from the moon, and -ly adds the repeating rhythm of the moon cycle, so monthly means once per moon cycle.
senses.whyCN: month 源自月亮，-ly 加上月亮周期的重复节奏，所以 monthly 就是「每轮月亮绕一圈发生一次」。

senses.title: Paid or charged by the month
senses.definition: paid, charged or reported for a period of one month
senses.definitionCN: 按一个月的周期付款、收费或结算的
senses.example: She switched to a monthly plan to save money.
senses.exampleCN: 为省钱她改用按月付费的套餐。
senses.why: Once the word marks a month as a unit, it naturally describes money and reports measured in months.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词把一个月当成了计量单位，它自然就用来修饰按月份计算的金额和报表。

senses.title: A magazine published each month
senses.definition: a magazine or newspaper that is published once a month
senses.definitionCN: 每月出版一次的杂志或报刊
senses.example: The science monthly printed her letter in March.
senses.exampleCN: 那本科学月刊在三月刊登了她的读者来信。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the thing itself, so a publication issued monthly can be called a monthly.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了名词指代事物本身，于是每月出一次的刊物可以被直接叫作 monthly，即月报月刊。

senses.title: Once every month
senses.definition: used as an adverb to say that something happens once each month
senses.definitionCN: 作副词表示某事每月发生一次
senses.example: The committee meets monthly to review the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每月开会审核预算。
senses.why: English often adds -ly to turn time words into adverbs, so monthly can describe how often an action happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 -ly 把时间词变成副词，因此 monthly 能表示动作发生的频率。

senses.title: Related to the moon
senses.definition: used in old or technical contexts to describe something connected with the moon
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧或专业的语境中，指与月亮有关的
senses.example: Ancient farmers followed a monthly calendar tied to the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 古代农夫使用与月亮相关的月历。
senses.why: Month and moon share the same Germanic root, so monthly keeps a faint lunar meaning that survives in lunar calendars.
senses.whyCN: month 与 moon 共享同一个日耳曼词根，因此 monthly 保留了淡淡的月亮含义，在太阴历中仍可见。

senses.title: A menstrual period
senses.definition: a period of menstruation, used in informal British English, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 月经，常用于英式口语，通常用复数形式
senses.example: The doctor asked when her last monthly had been.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问她上一次月经是什么时候。
senses.why: Because menstruation repeats roughly once a month, the frequency word became a discreet name for it.
senses.whyCN: 因为月经大约每月重复一次，这个表示频率的词就成了对月经的委婉称呼。

intro.en: Monthly is formed in English from month plus -ly, and month descends from Old English monath, tied to the word for moon.
intro.cn: monthly 是英语内部由 month 加 -ly 构成的词，而 month 源自古英语 monath，与表示月亮 mōna 的词同源。

items.en: The reconstructed form menothz names a month, probably from the moon cycle.
items.cn: 重构形式 menothz 意为「月」，一般认为与月亮周期有关。

items.en: Monath means a month, and Mona names the moon, so the two words were close kin.
items.cn: 古英语 monath 意为「月」，mōna 指月亮，两词关系密切。

items.en: Moneth settles into the later spelling month through the 13th to 15th centuries.
items.cn: 中古英语 moneth 在十三到十五世纪间逐渐定型为今天的 month。

items.en: Monthly appears as both adjective and adverb, built by adding -ly to the noun.
items.cn: monthly 作为形容词和副词出现，都是在名词后加 -ly 构成的。

items.en: Periodical publishing gives monthly the noun sense of a magazine issued each month.
items.cn: 期刊出版让 monthly 获得名词义，指每月出版的杂志。

items.en: Modern English uses monthly mostly for money, reports, meetings and magazines, rarely for the moon.
items.cn: 现代英语中 monthly 多用于金钱、报表、会议和杂志，已很少指月亮。

note.en: Monthly looks like the family words month, bimonthly and fortnightly, and sits near the frequency words annual, weekly and lunar.
note.cn: monthly 在拼写与构词上与 month、bimonthly、fortnightly 等词族相邻，在意义上与 annual、weekly 等频率词接近。

entries.definition: one of the twelve periods of the year
entries.definitionCN: 一年十二个月中的一个月

entries.definition: lasting for one month
entries.definitionCN: 持续一个月的

entries.definition: every two months, or twice a month
entries.definitionCN: 每两月的；每月两次的（两种意思都有，需看语境）

entries.definition: every two weeks
entries.definitionCN: 每两周的（与 monthly 同为 -ly 频率形容词）

entries.definition: happening once a year
entries.definitionCN: 每年的；一年一次的

entries.definition: happening once a week
entries.definitionCN: 每周的；每周一次的

entries.definition: connected with the moon
entries.definitionCN: 月亮的；与月亮相关的

normalIntro.en: Monthly is simply month plus the suffix -ly, and month itself goes back to the moon, whose cycle marks one turn of the calendar.
normalIntro.cn: monthly 就是 month 加后缀 -ly；而 month 又可追溯到月亮，月亮的一个周期就是日历翻过的一页。

normal.en: The suffix -ly builds monthly from month just as it builds weekly from week.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ly 把 month 变成 monthly，就像把 week 变成 weekly 一样。

normal.en: Month and moon share a Germanic root, so lunar and monthly are cousins.
normal.cn: month 与 moon 共享日耳曼词根，所以 lunar 与 monthly 是亲戚。

normal.en: Monthly is adjective, adverb and noun in one form, so the context decides its job.
normal.cn: monthly 一身兼任形容词、副词和名词，具体身份由语境决定。

normal.en: Be careful with bimonthly, which can mean twice a month or every two months.
normal.cn: 要小心 bimonthly，它既可指每月两次，也可指每两个月一次。

normal.en: Common partners are monthly payment, monthly report and monthly magazine.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有 monthly payment、monthly report 与 monthly magazine。

abstract.en: Watch a calendar page turn while the moon completes one circle.
abstract.cn: 想象日历翻过一页的同时，月亮正好走完一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a small envelope arriving on the kitchen table with a bill inside.
abstract.cn: 想象厨桌上每月准时到来的一个装账单的小信封。

abstract.en: Think of a clock with a hand that points to a new magazine cover each time it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟的指针每动一格，就指到一期新的杂志封面。

examples.en: The bank deducts the monthly interest on the last working day.
examples.cn: 银行在最后一个工作日扣除当月利息。

examples.en: The society publishes a monthly for young naturalists.
examples.cn: 该协会为年轻博物爱好者出版一本月刊。

examples.en: Team leaders report monthly on how the projects are progressing.
examples.cn: 各团队负责人每月汇报项目进展。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「忙死丽」——太忙了，只好每月才见一次面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 原始日耳曼语 menothz（月，一般认为与月亮周期有关）→ 古英语 monath（月）→ 中古英语 moneth → month → 加 -ly 构成 monthly（每月的）。

sensesIntro.en: Monthly begins as a frequency word for once a month, extends to money and reports measured by the month, becomes a noun for a monthly magazine, works as an adverb, keeps an old lunar link, and finally serves as an informal name for a menstrual period.
sensesIntro.cn: monthly 首先是表示「每月一次」的频率词，再扩展到按月份结算的钱款与报表，又转化为指月刊的名词，还能作副词，并保留了与月亮的旧联系，最后在口语中成为月经的委婉说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page turning under a full moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：月光下日历翻过一页。

branches.en: Frequency is the basic sense, in adjective and adverb form.
branches.cn: 频率是本义，兼具形容词与副词用法。

branches.en: Money and reports turn the frequency into a billing unit.
branches.cn: 金钱与报表把频率变成了结算单位。

branches.en: The publication is the frequency word used as a noun.
branches.cn: 刊物是频率词直接转成的名词。

branches.en: The lunar link is the oldest trace, once the root of the word.
branches.cn: 与月亮的联系是最古老的痕迹，曾是这个词的根。

branches.en: The same once-a-month idea becomes a discreet everyday label.
branches.cn: 同一个「每月一次」的想法变成了一种委婉的日常说法。

intro.en: Monthly is a plain English formation: the noun month plus the suffix -ly, with family words monthlong and bimonthly.
intro.cn: monthly 是典型的英语构词：名词 month 加后缀 -ly，词族有 monthlong 与 bimonthly。

latinIntro.en: Latin offers no direct ancestor here; month is a Germanic word, and the nearest Latin relatives are mensis, a month, and luna, the moon.
latinIntro.cn: monthly 没有直接源自拉丁语的祖先：month 是日耳曼词，最接近的拉丁亲属是 mensis（月）与 luna（月亮）。

items.meaning: a period of about four weeks
items.example: Month is the base of the whole word family.
items.exampleCN: month 是整个词族的基础。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms frequency adjectives like weekly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 weekly 这类频率形容词。

items.example: The adverb -ly lets monthly describe how often something happens.
items.exampleCN: 副词性的 -ly 让 monthly 能说明动作发生的频率。

items.meaning: once a month, or a monthly magazine
items.example: Monthly covers all three parts of speech.
items.exampleCN: monthly 涉及三种词性。

items.example: The compound monthlong adds length, not frequency.
items.exampleCN: 复合词 monthlong 表示时长，不表示频率。

items.example: The prefix bi- makes bimonthly ambiguous.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 bi- 让 bimonthly 产生歧义。

items.meaning: every two months or twice a month
items.example: Bimonthly should be clarified in writing.
items.exampleCN: 写作中应把 bimonthly 的意思说清楚。

items.example: Fortnight gives fortnightly, a monthly-like interval.
items.exampleCN: fortnight 构成 fortnightly，是与 monthly 相近的间隔词。

items.meaning: person or thing that does something
items.example: Words like worker show person suffixes, unlike month.
items.exampleCN: worker 这类词带人称词尾，而 month 不带。

definition_zh: 士气；斗志；信心；精神面貌
definition_en: the level of confidence, enthusiasm and willingness to keep going that a person or a group shows at a particular time
core_image: 疲惫的队伍依然抬着头，眼里还燃着一团火
scene: 连续加班两周后，项目组的人依然凑在一起说笑，对接下来的评审很有底气。Despite the long hours, the team kept its morale high before the final review.
sceneCN: 这里 morale 是「士气」（第 1 个义项：群体在困境中保持的信心与斗志）；句意是尽管加班很久，团队在最终评审前依然士气高昂。

pos.zh: 名词：士气；斗志；信心；精神面貌

derivatives.zh: 由前缀 de-「去除」加本词词根构成，义为「使士气低落；使泄气」（美式拼作 demoralize）
demoralise 加 -ed 构成，义为「士气低落的；泄了气的」
demoralise 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人泄气的；打击士气的」
demoralise 加 -ation 名词后缀，义为「士气低落；意志消沉」
由同词根的 moral 加 -istic 构成，义为「说教的；道学气的」，与 morale 同源但强调道德评判

senses.title: Confidence that keeps a group going
senses.titleCN: 士气：群体撑下去的信心
senses.definition: the confidence, enthusiasm and willingness to work that members of a group feel together, especially when things are hard
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体成员共同持有的信心、热情与继续干下去的意愿，尤指困难时期
senses.example: Morale was high after the team won its first match.
senses.exampleCN: 球队赢下第一场比赛后，士气高涨。
senses.why: The French noun moral meant a set of settled ways of feeling, so morale names the shared spirit of a body of people rather than any one mind.
senses.whyCN: 法语名词 moral 原指一套稳定的感觉方式，因此 morale 指一群人共有的精神气，而不是某一个人的心情。

senses.title: The spirit of a single person
senses.titleCN: 一个人的精神状态；心气
senses.definition: the emotional and mental state of one person, showing how much fight or hope that person has left
senses.definitionCN: 单个人的情绪与心理状态，显示出他还剩下多少斗志或希望
senses.example: After months of rejections, his morale finally cracked.
senses.exampleCN: 被拒绝数月之后，他的精神终于垮了。
senses.why: The group sense narrowed to one person in ordinary British use, and dictionaries mark this narrower use as wordbook only, so the picture stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 群体义在日常英式用法里收窄到一个人身上，多部词典把这一较窄用法标为英式，画面不变，只是从一群缩成一个人。

senses.title: A feeling that spreads through a unit
senses.titleCN: 蔓延在集体里的情绪氛围
senses.definition: a collective emotional tone, such as fear or confidence, that passes from member to member inside an army unit, a workplace or a squad
senses.definitionCN: 在部队、职场或小队内部从成员到成员传染开来的集体情绪基调，如恐惧或自信
senses.example: A single rumour lowered morale across the whole battalion.
senses.exampleCN: 一则谣言让整个营的士气都低了下去。
senses.why: Because morale is felt by a group at the same moment, it behaves like a mood in the air that later comers can catch, which is why officers and managers watch it like weather.
senses.whyCN: 正因为 morale 是一群人在同一时刻感受到的，它就像一个悬在空气中的氛围，后来的人也能沾上，所以军官和经理都像看天气一样盯着它。

senses.title: The mental strength to keep going
senses.definition: a reserve of courage and determination that lets a person or a team carry on through exhaustion, danger or long failure
senses.definitionCN: 一种勇气与决心储备，让人或队伍在疲惫、危险或长期失败中仍能坚持
senses.example: The long march tested the soldiers, but it never broke their morale.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军考验了士兵，却没能摧毁他们的意志。
senses.why: The same word that names a bright spirit also names what is left of it after hard use, so morale becomes the store of firmness that can be run low.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指明亮的精神气，也指被耗用之后剩下的那部分，所以 morale 成了可以消耗见底的「硬气储备」。

senses.title: In military and workplace usage
senses.titleCN: 军事与职场语境中的士气
senses.definition: the level of this confidence that officers or managers actively assess, report on and work to keep up, as in troop morale or staff morale
senses.definitionCN: 军官或管理者主动评估、汇报并设法维持的信心水平，如「部队士气」「员工士气」
senses.example: The report warned that staff morale was falling after the budget cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 报告警告说，预算削减之后员工士气正在下滑。
senses.why: Where leaders are held responsible for the spirit of others, morale stops being a private feeling and becomes something measured and reported, often in company with staff or troop.
senses.whyCN: 当领导者要为别人的精神负责时，morale 就不再是私人感受，而变成被衡量、被汇报的东西，常与 staff 或 troop 一起出现。

senses.title: The set phrase about boosting
senses.definition: in common phrases such as boost morale or a morale booster, the movable quantity that good news, rest or encouragement adds to a team
senses.definitionCN: 在 boost morale、a morale booster 等常见说法中，指好消息、休息或鼓励为团队加上的那部分可以增减的量
senses.example: Winning the tournament gave the squad a real morale booster.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得锦标赛给了球队一次实实在在的士气提振。
senses.why: Once morale is pictured as a level that can be raised or lowered, English freely builds phrases in which it behaves like a supply with a tap.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把 morale 想象成一个可以被抬高或压低的水平，英语就能自由造出把它当成有开关的「供给」的说法。

intro.en: Morale looks like moral because both go back to a Latin adjective describing habit and custom; English borrowed the noun twice, once with an e and once without.
intro.cn: morale 与 moral 看起来几乎一样，因为两者都出自一个描述习惯与风俗的拉丁语形容词；英语把这名词借了两次，一次带 e，一次不带。

items.en: The adjective moralis described what concerned mores, the accepted customs of a people.
items.cn: 形容词 moralis 描述与 mores（一个民族公认的风俗习惯）有关的东西。

items.en: French turned the adjective into a noun, and the feminine form morale came to name the set of feelings and customs a group holds, especially in an army.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词变成名词，阴性形式 morale 逐渐指一个群体（尤其是军队）所持的整套情感与习惯。

items.en: French officers spoke of the morale of a unit, meaning the confidence and spirit of the men rather than their weapons or numbers; this sense is the one English borrowed.
items.cn: 法语军官谈论一支队伍的 morale，指的不是武器或人数，而是士兵的信心与精神；英语借的就是这一义。

items.en: English took the noun with its final e in the eighteen-thirties, mostly through military writing, while the older word moral stayed with questions of right and wrong.
items.cn: 英语在一八三〇年代带着末尾的 e 借入这个名词，多经由军事写作；更早的 moral 则继续保留「是非对错」之义。

items.en: The e kept the two nouns apart on the page; dictionaries now note that the single-person sense of morale is mainly British usage, and the exact first dates for these uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 末尾的 e 让两个名词在书面上分开；现在词典注明 morale 表示「单个人精神」的用法主要见于英式英语，这些用法的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English extends morale from armies to offices, hospitals and sports teams, where it is judged by how much a group still wants to show up.
items.cn: 现代英语把 morale 从军队扩展到办公室、医院和运动队，衡量的都是这个群体还愿不愿意继续出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin noun for customs, including the lookalike moral; the near-meaning group gathers words for spirit, frame of mind and spirits, which differ in who holds the feeling and how long it lasts.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「风俗」名词构成的一族词，包括极易混淆的 moral；近义组收表示精神气、情绪底色与兴致的词，区别在于感受由谁持有、又能持续多久。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun about right and wrong behaviour, not about confidence; it shares the Latin root for customs with morale.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「道德的；寓意」，与自信无关；它与 morale 共享表示「风俗」的拉丁语词根，只差末尾一个字母。

entries.definition: The noun for principles of right and wrong conduct, formed from moral rather than from morale.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「道德；道德准则」，由 moral 而非 morale 构成，与 morale 同源但谈论的是对错。

entries.definition: To take away the confidence and spirit of a person or a group, formed with the prefix de- meaning removal.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使士气低落、使泄气」，由表「去除」的前缀 de- 加本词词根构成，是本词最直接的派生词。

entries.definition: Courage and liveliness of mind; close to morale, but it can be completely personal and does not always belong to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精神；气概」，与 morale 很近，但可以完全是个人的，并不一定属于一个群体。

entries.definition: A temporary state of feeling that can shift in an afternoon; shorter-lived than morale and not tied to a task.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「心情；情绪」，是一种可能一下午就会变的状态，比 morale 短暂，也不与任务挂钩。

entries.definition: The guiding beliefs and character of a group; slower to change than morale and describes identity rather than current confidence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精神气质；群体信念」，比 morale 变化更慢，描述的是身份共识而非当下的信心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin noun for customs, the lookalike moral, and the phrases that morale actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「风俗」名词、容易混淆的 moral，以及 morale 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Morale keeps the e, moral does not: the e keeps the spirit of a group apart from questions of right and wrong.
normal.cn: morale 保留词尾的 e，moral 没有：这个 e 把群体的精神气与是非对错分开。

normal.en: Both words come from Latin mores, the customs of a people, so morale is literally the habit a group has of keeping its chin up.
normal.cn: 两个词都出自拉丁语 mores（一个民族的风俗），因此 morale 字面上就是一群人抬着头的那股习惯。

normal.en: Boost morale is the everyday verb of choice; raise, lift and keep up morale also work, but boost is the strongest.
normal.cn: boost morale 是日常首选动词；raise、lift、keep up morale 也都能用，但 boost 语气最强。

normal.en: Low morale and falling morale are the common negative phrases, and they often sit beside staff, troop or team.
normal.cn: low morale 与 falling morale 是常见的负面说法，常与 staff、troop 或 team 搭配。

normal.en: Demoralise is the prefix de- taking the spirit away, so a demoralised squad is a squad whose morale has been pulled down.
normal.cn: demoralise 是前缀 de- 把精神气拿走，因此 demoralised squad 就是 morale 被压下去的队伍。

abstract.en: Picture a tired team in a long corridor: their shoulders are low, but their eyes still hold one bright thread of fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一支疲惫的队伍走在长走廊里：肩膀是垮的，眼里却还剩一缕明亮的火。

abstract.en: Imagine the spirit of a whole unit as weather over a camp that everyone shares at once.
abstract.cn: 把整个单位的精神气想象成压在营地上方、所有人同时经历的一片天气。

abstract.en: Think of a bar of light on a screen that a good piece of news slides upward for a whole afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条光带，一条好消息在下午把它缓缓推上去。

examples.en: The coach arranged a short weekend trip to keep morale up.
examples.cn: 教练安排了一次短暂的周末出游，以保持士气。

examples.en: Poor lighting and loud machinery had worn down the night shift, and their morale dropped within a month.
examples.cn: 昏暗的灯光和轰鸣的机器磨掉了夜班的劲头，一个月内他们的士气就下去了。

examples.en: A handwritten thank-you note proved to be a small but real boost to morale.
examples.cn: 一封手写的感谢信成了虽小却实在的士气提振。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸好啦」——全队摸清情况、拍肩打气，摸好了，士气就上来了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores，风俗、习惯）→ 形容词 moralis（关乎风俗与品行的）→ 古法语名词 moral、阴性 morale（情绪与风气）→ 十八世纪法语军事用语指部队的精神气 → 英语 morale 保留「群体精神气」义。注意 moral（道德）与 morale（士气）同源而不同义，末尾的 e 是区分的关键。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses move from the shared confidence of a group to the spirit of one person, to a feeling that spreads, to the strength that survives exhaustion, to the measured level in reports, and finally to the fixed phrases that raise it.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从群体的共同信心出发，收窄到单个人的精神，再扩展为传染性的氛围与扛过耗损的毅力，然后成为被评估与汇报的水平，最后定型为提升它的固定搭配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tired group still holding its heads up, with one bright thread of fire left in their eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支疲惫的队伍依然抬着头，眼里还留着一缕明亮的火。

branches.en: THE GROUP: the bright thread belongs to a team, a unit or an office at once.
branches.cn: 群体线：这一缕火光同时属于一支队伍、一个单位或一间办公室。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same thread can be found in one tired individual when a British speaker uses the narrower sense.
branches.cn: 个人线：当英式说法取其较窄的义项时，同一缕火光只出现在一个疲惫的个体身上。

branches.en: THE AIR: a rumour travels through a unit like weather, and morale spreads the same way.
branches.cn: 氛围线：谣言像天气一样在一支队伍里移动，morale 也是这样传开的。

branches.en: THE LEVEL: what survives the march becomes a level that officers and managers measure and report.
branches.cn: 水平线：行军之后剩下的部分变成一个水平，被军官和经理衡量与汇报。

branches.en: THE TAP: once the level is a supply, phrases such as boost morale turn it into something you can pour in.
branches.cn: 供给线：一旦这个水平被当成供给，boost morale 之类的说法就让它成了可以往里倒的东西。

intro.en: Morale is a Latin-derived noun for customs that French narrowed to the spirit of a body of people; English adds ordinary suffixes to build the family around the lookalike moral.
intro.cn: morale 是源自拉丁语、表示「风俗」的名词，法语把它收窄为一群人的精神气；英语再用普通后缀围绕形近的 moral 建起这一词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective moralis and its noun root mores are both recorded, so only the details of the French military sense are uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 moralis 与名词词根 mores 均有文献记录，来源存疑的只是法语军事义何时固定下来。

items.example: Mos is the custom of a people, and its plural is the heart of this family.
items.exampleCN: mos 是一个民族的风俗，它的复数形式是这一词族的核心。

items.example: The adjective describes what belongs to accepted conduct.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述属于公认行为规范的东西。

items.meaning: a settled way of feeling; a set of customs
items.meaningCN: 稳定的感受方式；一套风俗
items.example: The French noun is the direct parent of morale.
items.exampleCN: 法语的这个名词是 morale 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the spirit of a body of people
items.example: The French feminine form keeps the final e that English later borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 法语阴性形式保留了末尾的 e，英语后来连它一起借走。

items.example: The prefix de- takes the spirit out of demoralise.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 把精神气从 demoralise 里拿走。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns demoral into a verb, spelled -ize in American English.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把 demoral 变成动词，美式英语拼作 -ize。

items.example: The suffix forms moralistic, which describes someone given to preaching.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 moralistic，形容爱说教的人。

items.example: The suffix forms demoralisation, the state of lost spirit.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 demoralisation，指失去精神气的状态。

items.meaning: to take away confidence and spirit
items.example: Demoralise is the clearest sign of how morale behaves as a supply.
items.exampleCN: demoralise 最清楚地显示了 morale 像一种供给的特点。

items.meaning: inclined to preach about right and wrong
items.example: Moralistic shows the family turning toward judgement instead of spirit.
items.exampleCN: moralistic 显示了这一词族向了「评判」而不是「精神」的方向。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 风俗；习惯；复数指公认的规范

latinEntries.meaning: the accepted customs of a group

definition_zh: 道德；道德准则；道德体系；品行；道德性
definition_en: the set of beliefs about right and wrong behaviour that a person or a society holds, or the quality of acting according to them
core_image: 一群人围坐，把好赖是非一条条刻在同一块木牌上
scene: 讨论课上，同学追问法律与道德的界线究竟在哪里。The seminar asked whether a law can be right while the morality behind it is wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 morality 是「道德体系」（第 1 个义项：一套关于是非对错的信念）；句意是研讨课追问，一部法律会不会本身正确、而支撑它的道德体系却是错的。

pos.zh: 名词：道德；道德准则；道德体系；品行；道德性

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ity 后缀得到的基础词，形容词义为「道德的」，名词义为「寓意；道德准则」
由 moral 加 -ist「人」后缀构成，义为「道德家；说教者」
由 moral 加 -ise 动词后缀构成，义为「进行道德说教；使有德」（美式拼作 moralize）
由本词加否定前缀 im- 构成，义为「不道德；伤风败俗」
由否定前缀 a- 加 moral 构成，义为「非道德的；没有道德观念的」，与 immoral「不道德」不同

senses.title: Beliefs about right and wrong
senses.titleCN: 是非观念：一套道德信念
senses.definition: the set of beliefs that a person or group holds about what is right and wrong in behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体关于行为对错所持有的整套信念
senses.example: Her morality was shaped by the stories her grandmother told.
senses.exampleCN: 她的道德观念是祖母讲的那些故事塑造的。
senses.why: The Latin root names customs, and -ity turns a custom into a body of belief, so morality is the whole store of accepted rules rather than one rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根指「风俗」，-ity 把风俗变成一套信念，因此 morality 是被公认规则的整个仓库，而不是某一条规则。

senses.title: The standards of a whole society
senses.definition: the shared standards of conduct that a society, a profession or an age accepts and expects its members to follow
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会、一个行业或一个时代共同接受并要求成员遵守的行为标准
senses.example: Ideas of public morality have changed greatly over the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 公共道德的观念在近一个世纪里变化很大。
senses.why: Because customs belong to a people as a whole, the word naturally widens from one person to a society and even to a whole period.
senses.whyCN: 正因为风俗属于整个民族，这个词自然从一个人扩展到整个社会，甚至整个时代。

senses.title: The quality of being moral
senses.titleCN: 道德性：行为本身的对错属性
senses.definition: the quality that makes an action or a system right or wrong, as judged against a standard rather than against the law
senses.definitionCN: 使某个行为或制度在道德上成为对或错的那种属性，依据的是准则而非法律
senses.example: The debate turned on the morality of selling weapons to a country at war.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论的关键是把武器卖给交战国这件事本身是否合乎道德。
senses.why: When -ity is added to the adjective, the word can also name the abstract property of an act, which is why people argue about the morality of a policy.
senses.whyCN: 当 -ity 加在形容词之后，这个词也能指一种行为的抽象属性，所以人们才会争论某项政策的道德性。

senses.title: A system of ethics
senses.definition: an organised body of principles or theory about right conduct, often named by its author or its guiding idea
senses.definitionCN: 关于正当行为的有系统的原则或理论，常以其提出者或核心观念命名
senses.example: The course compares the morality of ancient and modern thinkers.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课比较古代与现代思想家的道德体系。
senses.why: Once morality is a store of rules, philosophers can collect, order and compare those rules, and the word becomes the name of a system.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 morality 成了一座规则仓库，哲学家就能把这些规则收集、排序、比较，这个词也就成了一个体系的名称。

senses.title: Behaviour judged as virtue or vice
senses.titleCN: 品行：按美德与恶行来评价的行为
senses.definition: the actual conduct of a person, often used with an adjective to say whether that conduct is good or bad
senses.definitionCN: 一个人实际的行为表现，常用形容词修饰，表示这种行为是好是坏
senses.example: The novel dwells on the morality of its characters, not the plot.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说关注的是人物的品行，而不是情节。
senses.why: The belief in right conduct shows up in what people actually do, so the abstract standard comes back down into daily behaviour as virtue or vice.
senses.whyCN: 关于正当行为的信念会显现在人实际做了什么上，于是这条抽象标准又落回日常行为，成为美德或恶行。

senses.title: Morality in plays and tales
senses.titleCN: 道德寓意：戏剧与故事里的教训
senses.definition: the lesson about good and bad conduct that a story, a play or a speech is meant to teach its audience
senses.definitionCN: 一个故事、一出戏或一篇讲话所要传达给读者的关于善恶行为的教训
senses.example: The old morality plays warned the audience not to give way to pride.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的道德剧提醒观众不要向骄傲低头。
senses.why: Where a story exists to teach conduct, the word shifts its job from naming the standard to naming the lesson the standard is told through.
senses.whyCN: 当一个故事的存在就是为了教人行事，这个词的职责便从命名标准转为命名那条借故事讲出来的教训。

intro.en: Morality is built on the Latin adjective for customs and conduct; the abstract ending -itas joined the Latin noun to English through French, and now names both a belief and a system of beliefs.
intro.cn: morality 建立在拉丁语表示「风俗与品行」的形容词之上；抽象后缀 -itas 把拉丁语名词经法语带进英语，如今既指一种信念，也指一套信念体系。

items.en: The adjective moralis described matters of custom and conduct, built on mos, whose plural mores means customs.
items.cn: 形容词 moralis 描述关乎风俗与品行的事物，由 mos 构成，其复数 mores 意为风俗。

items.en: The abstract noun moralitas is recorded meaning character or the quality of a thing, formed with the suffix -itas.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语有抽象名词 moralitas 的记载，意为品性或某物的性质，由后缀 -itas 构成。

items.en: Old French moralite carried the word into the learned language of its day, naming both right conduct and the lesson of a tale.
items.cn: 古法语 moralite 把这个词带入当时的文人语言，既指正当行为，也指故事里的教训。

items.en: English adopted the word in the fourteenth century, and the stage form morality play grew from the lesson sense; the earliest date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个词，舞台形式 morality play 正是从「教训」义发展而来，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English keeps morality for principles, conduct and the rightness of an act, while morale, its lookalike, went a separate way to mean spirit.
items.cn: 现代英语让 morality 负载原则、品行与行为对错之义，而其形近词 morale 则另走一路，表示精神气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same root for customs, including the easily confused morale; the near-meaning group gathers ethics, rules and virtue, which differ in whether they name a study, an agreed code or a personal good.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「风俗」词根构成的一族词，包括极易混淆的 morale；近义组收伦理、规则与美德，区别在于各自说的是学问、成文守则还是个人品德。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun from which morality is built, meaning concerned with right conduct or a lesson drawn from a story.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「道德的」或「寓意」，是 morality 的基础词，只需加上 -ity 就构成本词。

entries.definition: A near-identical word that means the confidence of a group, with no link to right and wrong; it only shares the same Latin origin.
entries.definitionCN: 与本词几乎同形的词，义为「士气」，与是非对错无关，只共享同一个拉丁来源，注意末尾的 e 与重音位置不同。

entries.definition: Directly opposite in meaning, describing conduct that breaks accepted moral standards.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不道德的」，描述违反公认道德标准的行为，是本词最直接的否定对照。

entries.definition: The study of moral principles, or the code of a profession; more formal and more theoretical than morality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伦理学；职业操守」，比 morality 更正式、更偏理论，也常指某一行业的守则。

entries.definition: A particular good quality in a person, such as honesty; morality names the whole standard, virtue names one good trait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「美德」，指个人身上的某种好品质，如诚实；morality 指整套标准，virtue 只指一种好品质。

entries.definition: A dramatic form of the fifteenth century in which characters stood for virtues and vices, teaching conduct to the audience.
entries.definitionCN: 复合词，义为「道德剧」，十五世纪的一种戏剧形式，角色分别代表美德与恶行，向观众传授行事之道。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin noun for customs, the lookalike morale, and the phrases morality actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「风俗」名词、容易混淆的 morale，以及 morality 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Moral is the adjective, and the ending -ity lifts it into a noun, so morality is the state or body of what is moral.
normal.cn: moral 是形容词，后缀 -ity 把它抬成名词，因此 morality 就是「道德的」那种性质或整体。

normal.en: Public morality, traditional morality and a sense of morality are the fixed phrases: morality is a standard that a public, a tradition or a sense holds.
normal.cn: public morality、traditional morality 与 a sense of morality 是固定说法：morality 是被公共、传统或感受所持有的一套标准。

normal.en: When you speak of the morality of a policy, you judge the act itself; when you speak of the morality of a person, you judge the person.
normal.cn: 说 the morality of a policy 时评价的是行为本身；说某人的 morality 时评价的是这个人。

normal.en: The prefix im- flips the word to immoral, which is one of the sharpest accusations in argument.
normal.cn: 前缀 im- 把单词翻成 immoral，这是辩论中最锋利的指控之一。

normal.en: Compare morale: morale ends in e and means spirit, morality ends in y and means right conduct.
normal.cn: 对比 morale：morale 以 e 结尾，指精神气；morality 以 y 结尾，指正当品行。

abstract.en: Picture a circle of people carving lines onto one wooden board, each line a rule they have agreed to keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人围坐，把一条条线刻在同一块木板上，每条线都是他们同意遵守的规则。

abstract.en: Imagine a society handing the same worn board down through generations, with some lines polished by touch and others freshly cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会把同一块磨旧的木板一代代传下去，有的线条被摸得发亮，有的则是新刻上去的。

abstract.en: Think of an act held up against that lit board: what the law allows can still cast a wrong shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象把一个行为举到那块被照亮的木板前对照：法律允许的事，投下的影子仍可能是歪的。

examples.en: She never questioned the rigid morality of the small town she grew up in.
examples.cn: 她从未质疑过自己长大的那个小镇那套严厉的道德。

examples.en: Philosophers still argue about the morality of breaking one promise to keep another.
examples.cn: 哲学家至今仍在争论：为守住一个承诺而违背另一个承诺，是否合乎道德。

examples.en: The teacher asked the class to compare the moralities of two cultures rather than rank them.
examples.cn: 老师让全班比较两种文化的道德体系，而不是给它们排名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸来题」——考试里摸来摸去的那道题，问的就是「这样做对不对」；光是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mos（复数 mores，风俗、习惯）→ 形容词 moralis（关乎风俗与品行的）→ 晚期拉丁语 moralitas（品性、性质）→ 古法语 moralite → 英语 morality。英语里 moral 是形容词与「寓意」名词，morale 是「士气」，三者同源而分工不同；后缀 -ity 表示状态与性质，故 morality 兼指「道德体系」与「行为的道德性」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses start from a person or group holding beliefs about right and wrong, widen to the standards of a society, become the abstract rightness of an act, turn into a system of ethics, come back to daily conduct as virtue or vice, and finally name the lesson a story teaches.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从个人或群体持有的是非信念出发，扩展为一个社会的行为标准，再抽象为行为本身的对错属性，成为一套伦理学体系，落回日常品行中的美德与恶行，最后指故事所传的教训。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people carving their rules for good and bad onto one shared wooden board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人围坐，把关于好与坏的一条条规则刻在同一块木板上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the board is what one mind keeps as its belief about right and wrong.
branches.cn: 个人线：这块木板是一个人心中的是非信念。

branches.en: THE GROUP: the same board is carved by a society, a profession or a school of thinkers and becomes their standard or system.
branches.cn: 群体线：同一块木板由一个社会、一个行业或一个学派刻成，成为它们的行为标准或体系。

branches.en: THE ACT: the board is held up against a single action to judge its rightness apart from the law.
branches.cn: 行为线：把木板举到某一个具体行为前，在法律之外判断它对不对。

branches.en: THE CHARACTER: daily conduct shows whether a person acts by the lines that were carved.
branches.cn: 品行线：日常言行显示一个人是否照着刻好的线条行事。

branches.en: THE STORY: a tale carries the board on stage and turns the rule into a lesson the audience can hear.
branches.cn: 故事线：一个故事把木板搬上舞台，把规则变成观众听得见的教训。

intro.en: Morality joins a Latin root for customs with the abstract noun suffix -ity; the same family supplies moral, morale, and several English prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: morality 由表示「风俗」的拉丁词根与抽象名词后缀 -ity 组合而成；同一词族还给出 moral、morale 以及若干英语前缀与后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin mos and mores are recorded, and so is the adjective moralis; the abstract noun exists in late Latin and its earliest English dates are uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mos 与 mores 以及形容词 moralis 均有文献记录；抽象名词在晚期拉丁语中即已出现，它在英语里的确切首见年代不确定。

items.example: Mos is the custom that morality is built on.
items.exampleCN: mos 是 morality 所依托的风俗。

items.example: The adjective gives the base form moral.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给出基础形式 moral。

items.example: The suffix -ity turns the adjective into the abstract noun morality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 把形容词变成抽象名词 morality。

items.example: Moral is the base from which the longer nouns grow.
items.exampleCN: moral 是长出更长名词的基础词。

items.example: The prefix im- forms immoral, meaning contrary to moral standards.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 构成 immoral，意为违反道德标准。

items.example: The prefix a- forms amoral, meaning lacking moral sense altogether.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 a- 构成 amoral，意为完全没有道德观念。

items.meaning: a person who does or follows
items.example: The suffix forms moralist, the person who preaches.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 moralist，指爱说教的人。

items.example: The suffix forms moralise, to act the preacher, spelled -ize in American English.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 moralise，意为做道德说教，美式拼作 -ize。

items.meaning: a person concerned with moral standards
items.example: Moralist shows the family turning toward judgement.
items.exampleCN: moralist 显示这一词族向「评判」方向生长。

items.meaningCN: 非道德的；无道德观念的
items.example: Amoral is not the same as immoral, which means actively wrong.
items.exampleCN: amoral 与 immoral 不同，后者指主动违背道德。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 风俗；习惯；复数指公认规范

latinEntries.meaning: the accepted customs of a group

definition_zh: 疾病的；患病的；病态的；阴森的；阴沉怪异的
definition_en: showing an unhealthy interest in death, disease or other grim subjects, or connected with disease itself
core_image: 一间病房里，病人盯着自己的病看个没完没了
scene: 病房窗外阳光正好，可病人总盯着自己的病历一页页翻，越看越沉。He kept reading about diseases online until his interest became morbid.
sceneCN: 这里 morbid 是「病态的」（第 3 个义项：对疾病、死亡等阴暗事物有不健康的兴趣）；句意是他不断在网上查疾病，直到这种兴趣变得病态。

pos.zh: 形容词：疾病的；病的；病态的；阴暗的；与病有关的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 名词后缀构成，义为「发病率；病态」
由本词加 -ly 副词后缀构成，义为「病态地」
由本词加 -ness 名词后缀构成，义为「病态；病状」
由同词根 morbid 加 -ific「产生……的」构成，义为「致病的」
同词根的阴性复数名词，义为「麻疹」，医学拉丁语仍在沿用

senses.title: Connected with disease
senses.definition: relating to or caused by a disease, especially in medical or technical descriptions of tissue and symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 与疾病有关的或由疾病引起的，尤用于对组织与症状的医学或技术描述
senses.example: The scan showed a morbid change in the tissue around the joint.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示关节周围的组织发生了病变。
senses.why: Latin morbus is simply disease, and the suffix -idus means tending towards, so the word begins as a plain medical label for anything of the sick body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 morbus 就是「疾病」，后缀 -idus 表示「倾向于」，因此这个词最初只是给病体上的一切贴上医学标签。

senses.title: Caused by or showing illness
senses.definition: arising from illness or showing the signs of it, such as the pale flush of a sick body
senses.definitionCN: 由疾病引起的或显露出疾病迹象的，例如病体上苍白泛红的样子
senses.example: Her cheeks had the morbid flush of a long fever.
senses.exampleCN: 她双颊泛着高烧不退的那种潮红。
senses.why: From describing where a symptom comes from, the word moves to describing how a body looks when disease is doing the work, and morbid becomes a quality of the sick.
senses.whyCN: 从描述症状的来处，这个词转而描述疾病发作时身体看起来的样子，morbid 于是成了病体的一种属性。

senses.title: An unhealthy interest in grim things
senses.titleCN: 病态的：对阴暗事物有不健康的兴趣
senses.definition: showing a strange and unhealthy interest in death, suffering or other dark subjects, in a way that goes beyond ordinary curiosity
senses.definitionCN: 对死亡、痛苦等阴暗主题表现出古怪而不健康的兴趣，超出了普通的好奇
senses.example: The crowd slowed down to stare at the wreck with morbid curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 人群放慢脚步，带着病态的好奇看向那场碰撞。
senses.why: The disease image is folded inward: what is sick in the body becomes what is sick in the mind, so an interest itself can be diagnosed as morbid.
senses.whyCN: 疾病的意象被折向内部：身体上病的东西变成心里病的东西，于是一种兴趣本身也会被诊断为「病态」。

senses.title: Gloomy and unhealthy in tone
senses.titleCN: 阴森的：气氛与色调不健康
senses.definition: used of art, scenes or moods that are dark, unhealthy or brooding, as though sickness hung in the air
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容艺术、场景或情绪，阴暗、不健康、沉郁，仿佛空气里悬着病气
senses.example: The novel spends whole chapters in the morbid gloom of closed rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说整整几章都困在紧闭房间那种病态的阴暗里。
senses.why: Once the word can call an interest sick, it can also call the atmosphere around that interest sick, which gives it a strong literary tone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能说某种兴趣是病的，也就能说那种兴趣周围的气氛是病的，这给了它浓厚的文学色彩。

senses.title: The subject of disease and death
senses.titleCN: 疾病与死亡的阴暗题材
senses.definition: the grim subject matter of illness and dying, as named in such phrases as morbid anatomy and morbid thoughts
senses.definitionCN: 疾病与濒死这类阴暗题材，见于「病理解剖」与「病态的念头」等说法中
senses.example: Morbid anatomy was the old branch of study that examined the bodies of the dead.
senses.exampleCN: 病理解剖是专门检查死者遗体的学科。
senses.why: The word keeps the two halves of its history together: the body of the dead is examined medically, while the thought of the dead is examined morally.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把历史上的两半合在一起：死者的身体被医学方式检查，对死者的念头则被道德眼光审视。

senses.title: The formal sense of disease
senses.definition: in formal and medical writing, any disease or pathological condition, as in the noun morbidity that counts how often an illness appears
senses.definitionCN: 在正式与医学写作中泛指任何疾病或病理状态，如名词 morbidity 统计疾病出现的频率
senses.example: The report tracked the rates of disease in the district over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 报告追踪了该地区十年间的发病率。
senses.why: Latin morbus never left the word, so under all the dark overtones the plain medical sense is still there whenever doctors or officials count illness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 morbus 从未离开这个词，因此无论上面盖了多少阴暗的色彩，医生或官员清点疾病时，平实的医学义始终还在。

intro.en: Morbid comes straight from a Latin adjective built on the noun for disease; English first used it for physical illness and only later for a sick interest in grim things.
intro.cn: morbid 直接来自一个以「疾病」名词构成的拉丁语形容词；英语先用它说身体的病，后来才用它说对阴暗事物的病态兴趣。

items.en: The Latin noun morbus is often connected with a root for death, but the deeper history of the form is uncertain in its source and the usual link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 morbus 常被认为与表示「死亡」的词根相联，但这个词形更深的历史来源不确定，常见的联系属于重构形式。

items.en: Morbus is the ordinary Latin word for a disease, and the adjective morbidus meant sickly or diseased.
items.cn: morbus 是拉丁语中最普通的「疾病」词，形容词 morbidus 意为「有病的、患病的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century for medical and scientific description, first of all of the body of the sick.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪为医学与科学描述借入这个形容词，最初说的都是病者的身体。

items.en: By this time the word had also begun to describe what belongs to death, giving phrases such as morbid anatomy, which examined the dead.
items.cn: 到这时，这个词也已经开始描述属于死亡的事物，如病理解剖 morbid anatomy 要检查的就是死者。

items.en: Modern English most often uses morbid as a warning that an interest itself is unhealthy, so a morbid curiosity says something about the mind rather than the body.
items.cn: 现代英语最常用 morbid 提醒某种兴趣本身不健康，因此 morbid curiosity 说的是心理而不是身体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin noun for disease, together with one lookalike from a different verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for sick, unhealthy and grim, which differ in how literally bodily they are.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语「疾病」名词构成的一族词，包括容易混用的同根形容词与医学术语；近义组收「有病的、不健康的、阴森的」一类词，区别在于它们有多贴近身体本身。

entries.definition: The noun built from morbid, meaning the rate of disease in a group or the state of being unhealthy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发病率；病态」，由 morbid 加 -ity 构成，是医学统计里的常用词。

entries.definition: The medical Latin plural for measles, a surviving relative of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 医学术语，义为「麻疹」，是同一词族在医学拉丁语里的存留成员。

entries.definition: Merely similar in spelling: it means close to death or dying out, and comes from a Latin verb for dying, not from morbus for disease.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同：moribund 义为「垂死的；行将消亡的」，出自表示「死亡」的拉丁语动词，而不是表示「疾病」的 morbus。

entries.definition: Affected by illness; it is the plain everyday word, with none of the dark interest that morbid carries.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「生病的」，是日常平实说法，没有 morbid 那种对阴暗事物感兴趣的味道。

entries.definition: Having a disease in a body or a part of one; strictly medical and never used for a state of mind.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「患病的；病态的」，严格用于身体或其某一部分，不用于描述心境。

entries.definition: Taking a shocking and unpleasant pleasure in death or disaster; close to the dark sense of morbid but blunter.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「嗜血的；令人毛骨悚然的」，指从死亡或灾难中取乐，与 morbid 的阴暗义接近但语气更直白。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin noun for disease, the related nouns and adjectives, and the phrases morbid actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「疾病」名词、相关名词与形容词，以及 morbid 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Morbus is the Latin word for disease, so morbid is the adjective of disease: anything of the sick body starts here.
normal.cn: morbus 是拉丁语「疾病」一词，因此 morbid 就是「疾病的形容词」：属于病体的一切都从这里出发。

normal.en: Morbidity is the noun beside it, and doctors use the word to count how much disease a place has.
normal.cn: morbidity 是与它配套的名词，医生用这个词来统计一个地方的疾病有多少。

normal.en: Morbid curiosity is the fixed phrase for an interest that is itself sick, with morbid obsession and morbid fascination close beside it.
normal.cn: morbid curiosity 是「本身也是病的兴趣」的固定说法，morbid obsession 与 morbid fascination 意思相近。

normal.en: The same family gives the medical adjective morbific, meaning disease-causing, so -ific marks the one that brings illness.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出医学形容词 morbific，意为「致病的」，所以 -ific 标记的是「带来疾病」的那一个。

normal.en: Do not confuse morbid with moribund: morbidity is about disease, while moribund is about dying.
normal.cn: 不要把 morbid 和 moribund 混为一谈：morbi- 谈的是疾病，moribund 谈的是垂死。

abstract.en: Picture a sickroom where the patient stares at the illness in the mirror instead of the window.
abstract.cn: 想象一间病房，病人对着镜子盯住身上的病，而不是去看窗户。

abstract.en: Imagine that stare turning outward, until the same person reads every illness story just to feel the chill.
abstract.cn: 想象那道目光转向外面，直到这个人只是为了发冷而去读每一则疾病新闻。

abstract.en: Think of a grey corridor of closed rooms where the air itself seems infected.
abstract.cn: 想象一条灰色走廊，两旁房门紧闭，仿佛连空气都染了病。

examples.en: Some readers come to the true-crime shelf out of morbid curiosity and leave with a strange calm.
examples.cn: 有些读者带着病态的好奇走向真实犯罪书区，离开时却带着一种奇怪的平静。

examples.en: Doctors treat morbidity rates as a measure of how common disease is in an area.
examples.cn: 医生把发病率当作衡量一个地区疾病普遍程度的指标。

examples.en: The old house had a morbid quality that nothing in the bright garden could dispel.
examples.cn: 那座老屋有一种病态的气息，明亮的庭院无论怎样也驱不散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「猫病」——猫生了病，看着主人眼神怪怪的；把 morbid 记成「猫有病→病态的」，只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 morbus（疾病）→ 形容词 morbidus（有病的、患病的）→ 十七世纪英语借用，先用于医学描述 → 十八、十九世纪扩展到死亡与病者的身体（如病理解剖）→ 现代英语转而形容对阴暗事物的病态兴趣。更早的印欧语来源不确定，常见的「与死亡词根相联」说法只是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses start from the plain medical sense of belonging to disease, pass to the sick look a disease gives a body, turn inward into an unhealthy interest in death, settle into a gloomy tone, name the grim subject matter of disease and dying, and end back at the formal word for illness itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项从「属于疾病」这一平实的医学义出发，移到疾病给身体带来的病态外观，转向内部成为对死亡的不健康兴趣，落成阴郁的语调，指疾病与死亡的阴暗题材，最后又回到「疾病」本身的正式说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sickroom where the patient keeps looking at the illness rather than out of the window.
core.cn: 核心意象：病房里，病人反复盯着身上的病，而不是望向窗外。

branches.en: THE BODY: morbus is disease, and morbid is the adjective that names anything belonging to it.
branches.cn: 身体线：morbus 是疾病，morbid 则是命名一切属于疾病之物的形容词。

branches.en: THE APPEARANCE: the same disease shows on the skin and the eyes, and the word names that sick look.
branches.cn: 外观线：同一种病会显现在皮肤与眼神上，这个词便命名那种病态的样子。

branches.en: THE MIND: the stare turns inward, and an interest in death is itself diagnosed as sick.
branches.cn: 心理线：目光转向内部，对死亡的兴趣本身就被诊断为病。

branches.en: THE ATMOSPHERE: the sick mind spreads into art, scenes and moods, which become gloomy and unhealthy.
branches.cn: 氛围线：病态的心蔓延到艺术、场景与情绪里，它们因此变得阴郁而不健康。

branches.en: THE RECORD: the disease and the dead stay as subject matter, and morbidity counts them in clinical reports.
branches.cn: 记录线：疾病与死者留作题材，而 morbidity 在临床报告里把它们计数。

intro.en: Morbid is a Latin adjective built on the noun for disease; English adds ordinary suffixes to make one of the clearest families in medical vocabulary.
intro.cn: morbid 是由「疾病」名词构成的拉丁语形容词；英语再加上普通后缀，使它成为医学词汇中词族最清楚的一个。

latinIntro.en: Latin morbus and morbidus are both recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European connection belongs to reconstructed forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 morbus 与 morbidus 均有文献记录，属于重构形式的只是更早的印欧语关联。

items.example: Morbus is the disease noun under every member of this family.
items.exampleCN: morbus 是这一词族每个成员底下的「疾病」名词。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source of English morbid.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词就是英语 morbid 的直接来源。

items.meaning: tending to, in a state of
items.example: The ending -id marks the adjective of state, as here.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 标示状态形容词，本词正是如此。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms morbidity, the rate of disease.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 morbidity，指疾病的比率。

items.example: The suffix forms morbidly, as in morbidly obese.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 morbidly，如 morbidly obese 病态肥胖。

items.example: The suffix forms morbidness, a rarer synonym of morbidity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 morbidness，是 morbidity 较少见的同义说法。

items.example: The suffix forms morbific, which means disease-causing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 morbific，意为「致病的」。

items.example: The ending belongs to moribund, a lookalike that is not from morbus.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾属于 moribund，是与本词形近但并非出自 morbus 的词。

items.meaning: the rate or state of disease
items.example: Morbidity appears beside mortality in public health reports.
items.exampleCN: morbidity 在公共卫生报告里与 mortality「死亡率」并列出现。

items.example: Morbidly often modifies adjectives about weight or humour.
items.exampleCN: morbidly 常修饰关于体重或幽默的形容词。

definition_zh: 垂死的；行将消亡的；停滞不前的
definition_en: nearing death, or about to end or lose all vitality
core_image: 病床上的老人：气息微弱，眼睛还睁着，却已不再看向未来
scene: 一家老牌报纸连续多年亏损，订户大批流失，评论家说它已经进入了末期。The old newspaper had lost most of its readers, and critics called it moribund.
sceneCN: 这里 moribund 是「行将消亡的」（第 2 个义项：机构或制度走向终结）；句意：这家老报纸失去了大部分读者，评论家说它已垂死。

derivatives.zh: 垂死的状态；将死的境况
濒死般地；没精打采地

senses.title: Close to death
senses.definition: in the last stage of life and likely to die soon
senses.definitionCN: 处于生命的最后阶段，很可能很快死去
senses.example: The doctors could do nothing for the moribund patient.
senses.exampleCN: 医生对这位垂死的病人无能为力。
senses.why: The Latin moribundus is built on mori, to die, so the word literally means dying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 moribundus 源自 mori（死），所以这个词字面上就是「正在死」。

senses.title: Coming to an end
senses.definition: used of an organization, system, or custom that is fading out and no longer works well
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容机构、制度或习俗走向终结、已无法正常运作
senses.example: The committee was moribund and met only once a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会已经名存实亡，一年才开一次会。
senses.why: If an institution can be said to be dying, its final stage of life becomes its terminal decline.
senses.whyCN: 既然机构也能被说成「正在死」，它的最后阶段就变成了难以挽回的衰亡。

senses.title: Lacking vigour
senses.definition: lacking energy, activity, or new ideas, though the thing still exists
senses.definitionCN: 虽仍存在，却缺乏活力、活动或新想法
senses.example: Economists worried about a moribund housing market.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家担心萎靡的房地产市场。
senses.why: A dying body hardly moves, so the word naturally stretches from dying to listless and stagnant.
senses.whyCN: 垂死的躯体几乎不再动，于是词义从「将死」自然引申为「毫无生气」。

intro.en: Moribund comes from Latin moribundus, which is formed from mori, to die.
intro.cn: moribund 来自拉丁语 moribundus，由 mori（死）构成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to die lies behind the Latin verb mori.
items.cn: 一般认为，拉丁语动词 mori 背后有一个表示「死」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Mori means to die, and moribundus means dying.
items.cn: mori 意为「死」，moribundus 意为「正在死的」。

items.en: The adjective moribundus spreads in legal and medical Latin for a person near death.
items.cn: 形容词 moribundus 在法律与医学拉丁语中用于指临近死亡的人。

items.en: English borrows moribund directly from Latin rather than through French.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 moribund，并不经过法语。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word extends from people to dying institutions.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词从人扩展到垂死的机构。

note.en: Moribund belongs to a Latin family of death words, and it stands near lethal, fatal, and dying.
note.cn: moribund 属于拉丁语中表示「死亡」的词族，语义上与致命的、垂死的词相邻。

entries.definition: certain to die one day
entries.definitionCN: 终有一死的；会死的

entries.definition: to humiliate or wound deeply
entries.definitionCN: 使羞辱；使难堪

entries.definition: living or lasting forever
entries.definitionCN: 不朽的；永生的

entries.definition: about to die or come to an end
entries.definitionCN: 将死的；临近结束的

entries.definition: becoming weaker or smaller over time
entries.definitionCN: 衰退的；下降的

entries.definition: causing death and leading to death
entries.definitionCN: 晚期的；致命的

normalIntro.en: Moribund is a Latin dying word: mori is to die, so moribund means in the act of dying.
normalIntro.cn: moribund 是一个拉丁语表「死」的词：mori 是死，所以它表示「正在死去」。

normal.en: The mort- family all goes back to Latin mortis, so mortal, mortify, and moribund are relatives.
normal.cn: mort- 词族都追溯到拉丁语 mortis，所以 mortal、mortify 与 moribund 是同族的。

normal.en: A moribund industry is one that is still on its feet but no longer growing.
normal.cn: moribund industry 指仍然撑着、却不再增长的产业。

normal.en: The -bund ending is linked to the Latin gerund formation, which gives a sense of ongoing process.
normal.cn: 词尾 -bund 与拉丁语动词的进行性表达有关，因此带有「正在发生」的意味。

normal.en: Compare moribund with dying: moribund is more formal and often describes institutions.
normal.cn: 把 moribund 与 dying 对比：moribund 更正式，常用来形容机构。

normal.en: A moribund patient in a novel usually receives a last visit from the heirs.
normal.cn: 小说里的 moribund patient 通常等来继承人的最后一次探病。

abstract.en: Picture a candle whose flame still shows but is almost out.
abstract.cn: 想象一根蜡烛火焰还在，却已几乎熄灭。

abstract.en: Imagine a train in the last minutes before it is taken out of service.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车在被退役前最后几分钟的运行。

abstract.en: Think of a shop window with the same display for a whole year.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店的橱窗一整年都没有换过陈列。

examples.en: The museum had become almost moribund before the new director arrived.
examples.cn: 在新馆长到来之前，这座博物馆已几乎名存实亡。

examples.en: Nurses kept the moribund man comfortable in his final hours.
examples.cn: 护士们让那垂死的男人在最后几个小时里舒适一些。

examples.en: He saw the club as moribund, with fewer members every year.
examples.cn: 他认为这个俱乐部已经奄奄一息，会员逐年减少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫里苯」——病人闻到一股药味，已垂危；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mori（死）+ -bundus（进行性形容词词尾）→ moribundus（正在死去的）→ 英语 moribund，核心义「走在死亡路上的」。

sensesIntro.en: Moribund starts with a person near death, widens to dying institutions, and then to any decaying thing that has lost its energy.
sensesIntro.cn: moribund 从一个人临近死亡开始，扩展到垂死的机构，再落实到失去活力的任何衰败之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flame that still shows but is almost out.
core.cn: 核心意象：火焰还在，却已几乎熄灭。

branches.en: The dying body is the original medical sense.
branches.cn: 垂死的身体是最初的医学义项。

branches.en: A dying institution keeps the same image of a last stage.
branches.cn: 垂死的机构沿用「最后阶段」这一意象。

branches.en: A thing that hardly moves is read as lacking vigour.
branches.cn: 几乎不再活动的东西就被读作缺乏活力。

branches.en: Both a patient and a club can be said to be at the end of their life.
branches.cn: 病人与俱乐部都可以说走到了生命的尽头。

branches.en: An institution that is dying is also one that has stopped growing.
branches.cn: 走向消亡的机构，也往往是停止成长的那一个。

intro.en: Moribund is built from the Latin death family of mori, with English relations such as mortal.
intro.cn: moribund 由拉丁语表「死」的 mori 家族构成，英语中有 mortal 等同源亲属。

latinIntro.en: Latin mori means to die and moribundus means dying, the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mori 意为死，moribundus 意为正在死的，是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Mori supplies the root of death.
items.exampleCN: mori 提供「死」这一词根。

items.example: Moribundus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: moribundus 是直接来源。

items.example: The ending names a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾表示一个进程。

items.example: Mortal shares the death root.
items.exampleCN: mortal 共享「死」的词根。

items.example: The prefix im- denies death.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 否定「死」。

items.example: Mortify once meant to put to death.
items.exampleCN: mortify 早期意为致死。

items.example: Mortality counts the deaths.
items.exampleCN: mortality 统计死亡。

items.example: The noun names the state.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词表示状态。

definition_zh: 终有一死的；凡人的；致命的；不共戴天的
definition_en: certain to die one day, or causing death, or very intense
core_image: 沙漏：上面的沙一刻不停地往下漏，谁也无法让它倒过来
scene: 有人问天上的神像，既然是神，为何也会流泪。神话里给出了答案，神像也被雕成凡人的模样。Yet the sculptor carved the god with the face of a mortal man.
sceneCN: 这里 mortal 是「凡人的；终有一死的」（第 1 个义项：会死的人）；句意：可雕塑家却把这位神刻成了凡人的面孔。

derivatives.zh: 必死性；死亡率
致命地；极度地
不死的；不朽的
使羞辱；使难堪

senses.title: Certain to die
senses.definition: of a person or being, certain to die one day
senses.definitionCN: 指人或生命体终有一天会死去
senses.example: All mortals must accept the limits of life.
senses.exampleCN: 所有凡人都必须接受生命的局限。
senses.why: The Latin mortalis comes from mors, death, so a mortal being is one that death can claim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mortalis 来自 mors（死），所以凡物就是死亡迟早会收走的那一个。

senses.title: Causing death
senses.definition: causing or ending in death
senses.definitionCN: 导致死亡或以死亡告终
senses.example: He suffered a mortal wound in the last battle.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一场战斗里受了致命伤。
senses.why: If death is part of the word, it can also describe the blow that brings death.
senses.whyCN: 既然「死」是这个词的内核，它也能形容带来死亡的那一击。

senses.title: Extreme or deadly serious
senses.definition: used about anger, fear, or enmity that is extremely intense
senses.definitionCN: 形容愤怒、恐惧或敌意极其强烈
senses.example: The two families were mortal enemies for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家世世代代是不共戴天的死敌。
senses.why: A feud that could end in death becomes a manner of speaking for anything at life-and-death intensity.
senses.whyCN: 可能以死亡收场的仇怨，逐渐变成形容「以命相搏」程度的口语表达。

senses.title: An ordinary person
senses.definition: a human being, especially as opposed to a god or a great figure
senses.definitionCN: 指普通人，尤与神祇或大人物相对
senses.example: The champion was, after all, only a mortal.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冠军说到底也只是个凡人。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for everything that is subject to death, and therefore for everyone ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指所有会死之物，也就顺理成章地指普通人。

intro.en: Mortal goes back to Latin mortalis, an adjective from mors, death.
intro.cn: mortal 可追溯到拉丁语 mortalis，它是 mors（死）的形容词。

items.en: A reconstructed root for death is commonly assumed behind Latin mors.
items.cn: 一般认为，拉丁语 mors 背后有一个表示「死」的原始印欧语词根（重构形式）。

items.en: Mors means death, and mortalis means subject to death.
items.cn: mors 意为死，mortalis 意为会死的。

items.en: Mortel carries the word into French in the twelfth century.
items.cn: 十二世纪，mortel 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: English mortal names both what must die and what causes death.
items.cn: 英语 mortal 同时指必死者与致命之物。

items.en: The word also becomes a noun for human beings seen against gods.
items.cn: 这个词又作为名词，指与神相对的人类。

note.en: Mortal belongs to the Latin death family and stands close to lethal, fatal, and human words.
note.cn: mortal 属于拉丁语「死」词族，与致命、人类的字样相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 垂死的；行将消亡的

entries.definition: the state of being mortal
entries.definitionCN: 必死性；死亡率

entries.definition: a place where dead bodies are kept
entries.definitionCN: 太平间；殡仪馆

entries.definition: causing death or disaster
entries.definitionCN: 致命的；灾难性的

entries.definition: able to cause death
entries.definitionCN: 能致死的

entries.definition: relating to people rather than gods
entries.definitionCN: 人的；人类的

normalIntro.en: Mortal is shaped by Latin mors, death, and its relatives all cluster around the same idea.
normalIntro.cn: mortal 由拉丁语 mors（死）塑造，它的同族词都围绕同一个观念。

normal.en: The m- in mortality, mortify, and mortuary all signal death.
normal.cn: mortality、mortify、mortuary 里的 m 都提示「死」。

normal.en: Mortal danger and a mortal wound carry the same death meaning as the adjective.
normal.cn: mortal danger 与 mortal wound 都用「死」这层含义。

normal.en: Mortal enemies are foes whose hatred is as strong as life and death.
normal.cn: mortal enemies 指仇深如生死的敌人。

normal.en: A mere mortal is an ordinary person, not a god or a hero.
normal.cn: mere mortal 指普通人，不是神也不是英雄。

normal.en: Compare mortal with lethal: mortal often describes wounds, lethal describes poisons or weapons.
normal.cn: mortal 与 lethal 对比：mortal 常形容伤口，lethal 常形容毒药或武器。

abstract.en: Picture an hourglass that can never be turned over.
abstract.cn: 想象一只永远无法翻过来的沙漏。

abstract.en: Think of a red line drawn once by a sword and left on the ground forever.
abstract.cn: 想象剑在地上划出的一道红线，从此再没消失。

abstract.en: Imagine a god stepping down from a statue to look like the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象神从雕像里走下来，变成人群中的模样。

examples.en: Even kings are mortal and must bow to time.
examples.cn: 就连国王也会死，也必须向时间低头。

examples.en: The fall from the roof could have been a mortal one.
examples.cn: 从屋顶摔下的那一下本来可能致命。

examples.en: They had been mortal enemies since the quarrel over land.
examples.cn: 自从争夺土地之后，他们就结成了死敌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸头」——人摸着自己的头，想知道还能活多久，因为人终有一死；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mors（死，属格 mortis）+ -alis（形容词词尾）→ mortalis（会死的）→ 古法语 mortel → 英语 mortal，核心义「死亡所能触及的」。

sensesIntro.en: Mortal begins with the fact that living things must die, then names what causes death, then exaggerates it into deadly intensity, and finally becomes a noun for ordinary people.
sensesIntro.cn: mortal 先是「生命终将死去」这一事实，再指「带来死亡之物」，再夸张为「要命的强度」，最后转名词指普通人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an hourglass that can never be turned over.
core.cn: 核心意象：永远无法翻转的沙漏。

branches.en: Being subject to death is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 受制于死亡是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Bringing death is the active counterpart.
branches.cn: 带来死亡是对应的主动义项。

branches.en: Deadly intensity is the emotional extension.
branches.cn: 要命的强度是情感上的引申。

branches.en: The mortal as a noun means a human being.
branches.cn: 作名词时 mortal 指人。

branches.en: A mortal enemy threatens a mortal life with mortal hatred.
branches.cn: 死敌以要命的仇恨威胁着会死的生命。

intro.en: Mortal belongs to the Latin mort- family, which gives mortal, mortality, immortal, and mortify.
intro.cn: mortal 属于拉丁语 mort- 词族，由此构成 mortal、mortality、immortal 与 mortify。

latinIntro.en: Latin mors, genitive mortis, means death, and mortalis means subject to death.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mors（属格 mortis）意为死，mortalis 意为会死的。

items.example: Mors supplies the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: mors 提供这个词族的词根。

items.example: The suffix builds mortalis.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 mortalis。

items.example: Mortalis is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: mortalis 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix forms mortality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 mortality。

items.example: Mortality counts the deaths.
items.exampleCN: mortality 统计死亡。

items.example: The prefix im- negates death.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 否定「死」。

items.example: Immortal means free of death.
items.exampleCN: immortal 表示不死的。

items.example: The suffix forms mortally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 mortally。

items.example: Mortally describes a wound.
items.exampleCN: mortally 形容伤得极重。

items.example: The suffix forms mortify.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -fy 构成 mortify。
